This supports the itinerant Fermi-surface-nesting origin of q_IC over the local-moment double-cone mechanism, consistent with the paper's conclusion, though the itinerant model is a minimal tight-binding surrogate rather than a full DFT calc and the 0.42 vs 0.46 match is approximate.
meta.observable: incommensurate ordering wavevector q_IC (r.l.u. along c), as predicted (a) by the local-moment IC condition J_c1/J_c2=-4cos(2pi q_IC) and the spin-wave fit/canting stability, and (b) by the peak of the itinerant Lindhard susceptibility chi(q_z)

meta.conclusion: In the convective (Africa-like) rainfall-error regime, correcting the recent rainfall driver recovers more forecast skill (ΔKGE +0.114) than assimilating recent streamflow via EnKF (ΔKGE +0.072), and the two channels flip ranking between regimes (rainfall wins in convective, gauge wins in synoptic) — supporting the hypothesis that the Africa-Europe flood-skill gap is dominated by rainfall-driver error rather than gauge scarcity, though this is a controlled-simulator result not yet validated on real African basins.
meta.observable: Kling-Gupta Efficiency (KGE) of forecast streamflow vs truth at lead times 0-7 days, plus POD/FAR for 95th-percentile flood threshold exceedance; reported as mean over basins and forecast origins, and as channel recovery (ΔKGE = channel - baseline).

meta.conclusion: Device-level sub-threshold volatile switching DOES produce a cochlea-like tonotopic map: an analytic derivation gives log10(f_crit) exactly linear in applied voltage (R^2=1.00000) and a Monte-Carlo array maps log10(f) onto #ON with active-region R^2 up to 0.974 (0.82-0.97 across the robustness sweep), with log-spaced XOR channels — reproducing the paper's central empirical claim. However a rival-form test shows this log-linearity is GENERIC to steep sub-threshold switching tails (exp and logistic forms give R^2 within 0.001 of each other), NOT specific to volatile Ag/HfOx kinetics, so the distinctive-capability interpretation is only partly supported: the device-level computation works, but it is one instance of a broader mechanism class rather than a unique signature of volatility.
meta.observable: Tonotopic linearity: R^2 of #ON vs log10(f) (and the analytic log10(f_crit)-vs-V slope/R^2), the XOR-channel peak-frequency spacing, and the std(#ON)-vs-N_parallel scaling — i.e. the paper's own 'number of ON devices increases linearly with the logarithm of the input frequency' (Fig.3d) and 'each XOR shows a peak at a specific frequency' (Fig.4).

meta.conclusion: A multifault network geometry leaves a statistically significant imprint on the afterslip footprint on the LACUNARITY and TOPOLOGY (connected-component) metrics, but NOT robustly on anisotropy: once the single-fault null is made realistic (elliptical, rupture-directivity-bearing, rough boundary) it is itself anisotropic (ratio 1.64) — as anisotropic as the networks (1.37-1.39) — so anisotropy ratio does NOT distinguish single-fault from network. Lacunarity does (1.05 single vs 1.17-1.22 network, Cohen's d=2.2-2.8, p<3e-4), as does component count (1.0 vs 1.2-1.7). The honest finding: the multifault-vs-single distinction is detectable, but only via the gappy/multi-strand texture (lacunarity + components), not via footprint elongation — and weak-vs-strong network connectivity remains underpowered.
meta.observable: anisotropy ratio (PCA major/minor axis extent of the afterslip-derived aftershock-triggering footprint) and lacunarity (normalized gliding-box), with #connected-components and log(t) area-growth slope/R^2

meta.conclusion: In a UK-mortality-grounded competing-risks model, the QRISK3-style cause-specific framing overpredicts 10-year CVD risk relative to the true cumulative incidence by an age-dependent margin that is negligible below 60 (<0.5 pp) but reaches ~5 pp at 75-79 and ~10-11 pp at 80-84 with no extra predictors, and up to ~23 pp at 80-84 when the emerging QRISK3-omitted predictors (COPD, learning disability, Down syndrome, pre-eclampsia/postnatal depression) are present — driven mainly by COPD raising the competing non-CVD death hazard the naive estimate cannot see.
meta.observable: 10-year CVD cumulative incidence (CIF) vs the naive cause-specific (KM-style) 10-year risk, and their absolute difference in percentage points (overprediction gap)

meta.conclusion: Melting temperature and oxidation resistance are strongly anti-correlated across UHTC candidates (r=-0.81, 95%CI[-0.90,-0.71], P(slope<0)=1.0), and the single-objective 'highest Tm' screen fails at a realistic 1800 C oxidizing edge: every one of the three highest-melting materials (HfCN, HfC, TaC) is oxidation-limited and does NOT survive, while the Pareto-optimal HfB2-20SiC (lower Tm=3380 C) is the only candidate that does; this validates the hypothesis and confirms that hypersonic materials screening must be multi-objective (Pareto over Tm and oxidation resistance), not single-objective 'highest melting point'.
meta.observable: T_protect - the oxidation passivation ceiling, the temperature up to which a protective oxide scale is sustained against oxidizing air (the field's own observable for high-temperature oxidation resistance), regressed against melting temperature Tm; plus the survivability proxy T_survive = min(Tm, T_protect).

meta.conclusion: The consensus GBM state-state spatial interaction network is genuinely layerable: its exact minimum bandwidth is 5 (of 13, normalized 0.385) and is robust to leave-one-sample-out dropout (mean 5.9, 80% of drops <= the full-graph bandwidth), significantly below degree/density-matched random graphs (degree-preserving swap p=0.002, ER p=0.018), and my independent optimal ordering agrees with the paper's five-layer labels (Spearman 0.719, p=0.0038), tracing a hypoxia(MES.Hyp)->vascular->parenchyma(Neuron/Oligo) axis; however the layerability is only partly specific to the particular wiring — the configuration-model null (same degree sequence, randomized wiring) still reaches p=0.122, the disorganized region attains the same bandwidth=5 with fewer (23 vs 34) edges so bandwidth alone does not separate organized from disorganized tissue, and leave-one-out shows the SPECIFIC ordering is not uniquely determined (mean Spearman of resampled vs full order ~0, often negative), so the data robustly says 'layerable' but does not pin down a single canonical layer sequence.
meta.observable: minimum graph bandwidth (graph-bandwidth) of the consensus state-state spatial interaction network — the smallest, over all linear orderings of the 14 states, of the maximum positional span |pos(u)-pos(v)| of any consensus edge (u,v); reported raw and normalized by (n-1)=13. A band-limited graph (small bandwidth) is the formal criterion for the 'multi-layered' / within-or-adjacent-layer organization.

meta.conclusion: Joint high-density-plus-annotation modeling improves prediction over both alternatives: density is the dominant lever (full vs sparse +0.038 R^2 within, t=14.3) and annotations add a smaller but significant within-ancestry gain (+0.006, t=7.3); however, the annotation benefit is LARGER within-ancestry than cross-ancestry (within-cross = +0.0055), refuting my prediction that annotations would help MORE across ancestries.
meta.observable: out-of-sample prediction R^2 (squared Pearson correlation between PGS and phenotype), reported within-ancestry (EUR->EUR) and cross-ancestry (EUR-trained, EAS target).

meta.conclusion: Augmenting glm-5.2 with RDKit/PubChem chemistry tools raised objective chemistry-task accuracy from 0.727 to 0.909 (+0.182), with all 5 of the tool's unique wins concentrated in IUPAC naming and exact-molecular-weight computation — exactly the categories where a bare LLM must guess from memory and does so unreliably; the gain is directionally clear (5:1 discordant pairs) but, at n=22 scored tasks, is not statistically significant (exact McNemar p=0.22), so the claim is 'tools help on the failure-prone subtasks' rather than 'a guaranteed large overall gain.'
meta.observable: Per-task pass/fail (0/1) on objective chemistry checkers, summarized as accuracy = correct/total, overall and by category (name2struct, struct2name, properties, reaction); plus discordant-pair analysis.

meta.conclusion: Cyclo[13]carbon is computed (PBE0/def2-SVP geometry + CASSCF(4,4)/def2-SVP spin analysis) to have an OPEN-SHELL SINGLET ground state lying ~2.0 eV (2.03 eV at the singlet-relaxed kinked geometry, 1.05 eV at the triplet-relaxed cumulenic geometry, 2.58 eV comparing each state at its own relaxed geometry) below the triplet, with a polyynic, mirror-symmetric equilibrium structure carrying a single 'kink' defect (maximal BLA ~0.071 A at bond b6, swelling from the symmetry-equivalent ends toward the kink) forced by the odd ring size; the triplet, by contrast, prefers a perfectly cumulenic regular ring (no kink). Its covalent dimer cyclo[26]carbon is a true polyynic minimum (alternating 1.22/1.35 A, BLA 0.132 A, ~1.37 eV below the symmetry-trapped D26h cumulenic saddle), recovering the established even-cyclocarbon (C18-like) structure and confirming that odd-ring vs even-ring character is preserved through C13+C13 -> C26 dimerization; the cumulenic structure repeatedly obtained from a symmetric starting guess is shown to be a symmetry-trapped saddle, a non-trivial methodological finding.
meta.observable: singlet-triplet energy gap (eV) at relaxed geometry (CASSCF); bond-length alternation (BLA = max-min bond, Angstrom) and bond-length pattern (kink location/amplitude) of the optimized ring

meta.conclusion: Effective read depth is the single strongest driver of single-sample subclonal reconstruction accuracy (≈0.09 MCC per depth doubling, reproducing the paper's ~0.1); algorithm choice is significant but secondary (bic≈km > my dp implementation); and SNV-caller sensitivity drives accuracy only through its VAF-dependence (preferential loss of subclonal low-allele-fraction variants, beta=0.118, p=8.9e-9) — uniform dropout count has no effect — which refines, rather than contradicts, the paper's claim.
meta.observable: SC2A = Matthew's Correlation Coefficient (MCC) of pairwise mutation co-clustering (predicted vs true), the SMC-Het sub-challenge 2A hard-assignment metric; plus SC1B lineage-count score, SC2B co-clustering AJSD, SC1C cellular-prevalence error (MAE).

meta.conclusion: The hypothesis is supported at the kinase-centrality level but its naive gene-list form was falsified: only 18 of 62 active kinases are GBM-driver kinases, yet they carry 65.2% of all 2,268 phosphorylation edges in GBM driver pathways (z=5.72, p=5e-5 vs a size-matched random kinase-label null), with a scale-free substrate in-degree distribution (alpha=1.69) — meaning the PTM layer does converge onto an actionable driver-kinase-centered network, even though phospho-substrates are NOT enriched for GBM driver genes per se (fold-enrichment 0.74x) and substrates carry no excess PTM density (ratio 1.00x).
meta.observable: fraction of kinase->substrate phosphorylation edges attributable to GBM-driver kinases (vs size-matched random kinase-label null)

meta.conclusion: Self-supervised pathology pretraining (SimCLR on 100K H&E tiles) produces features that MATCH ImageNet transfer at full-data linear probing (0.848 vs 0.847 balanced accuracy) but DECISIVELY BEAT both random-init and ImageNet-supervised baselines in the few-shot regime (k=4: 0.845 vs 0.738 vs 0.578), with the advantage largest at the scarcest non-trivial data levels and a consistent rare-class (STR) advantage from k>=4 — supporting the foundation-model mechanism at ~4 orders of magnitude less data than Virchow, with the honest caveat that at the extreme single-shot (k=1) rare-class level ImageNet transfer still wins and the colorectal-only corpus proxies 'rare' with underrepresented tile classes rather than true rare cancer sites.
meta.observable: Few-shot balanced accuracy on CRC-VAL-HE-7K (overall + per-class, with emphasis on the smallest/rarest classes DEB n=339 and STR n=421) for each pretraining condition at k labeled shots per class; plus a full-data linear probe (train on 100K NCT tiles, test on 7180 CRC-VAL tiles) as the embedding-quality upper bound.

meta.conclusion: The H5/H1 globular domain binds the nucleosome on the dyad: across 9 solved chromatosome structures the median lateral displacement from the dyad axis is 1.19 A (1.04 A excluding one known off-dyad conformational state in 7K61), and an on-dyad-initialized MD trajectory stays at |y|~1.2-1.4 A over 10 ps. However, the on-dyad basin is laterally SHALLOW: +6 A and +10 A lateral nudges do not relax back to the dyad in the minimal vacuum/DNA-only model, indicating that on-dyad positioning is enforced by factors absent from this model (histone-core contacts, H5 C-terminal tail, solvent/ions, and the folding/assembly pathway) rather than by a deep electrostatic basin of the isolated globular domain on DNA.
meta.observable: lateral displacement |y| of the linker histone globular domain center from the nucleosome dyad axis (Angstrom, canonical dyad frame); plus the lateral drift of |y| under MD nudging as a basin-stability probe

meta.conclusion: The representation-learning taxonomy axis shows the expected empirical structure on a controlled series (silhouette 0.48, CONTR cleanly separated from the three reconstruction families) but collapses to chance (silhouette -0.04, p=0.51) on a real series where the contrastive family instead tracks the transformer family — so the axis is a real but dataset-fragile descriptor, not a robust behavioral invariant; the taxonomy is useful for organizing the field but should not be read as implying the families behave distinctly in practice.
meta.observable: taxonomy silhouette (reconstruction-axis vs representation-axis grouping) on the cross-family anomaly-score correlation-distance matrix

meta.conclusion: A model with an area-normalized CEI/side-reaction term and a separate grain-boundary isolation term reproduces the literature-pattern SC>PC retention advantage (9.5 pct pt unmatched) and, under matched BET area, retains ~73% of it (6.9 pct pt); a negative control with isolation disabled collapses the matched-BET advantage to exactly zero, showing the residual advantage is a genuine morphology (GB-isolation) effect rather than a pure surface-area artefact.
meta.observable: Capacity retention at cycle 100 (%, = Q100/Q0*100) and capacity fade per unit BET area at cycle 100 (mAh/m2)

meta.conclusion: A force-only-trained, fully-differentiable potential DOES yield analytical Hessians whose curvature STRUCTURE (which eigenvalue is negative -- i.e. saddle vs minimum) is correct in ~70-80% of clean-region geometries, and this learned Hessian drives a TS optimizer to a DFT-verified first-order saddle (in 18 steps, where the gradient-only baseline does not converge) -- so Denzel's pessimism is overcome qualitatively by smoothness/differentiability. BUT the learned Hessian is quantitatively unreliable (eigenvalue magnitudes off by factors of ~3-30, large error near repulsive walls), so this is partial support: the Hessian is usable as a curvature guide for TS location, not yet as an accurate vibrational/spectroscopic Hessian, and its quality tracks the model's local fit -- exactly the smoothness dependence Denzel's concern implies.
meta.observable: analytical Hessian of the trained potential via torch.autograd.functional.hessian on E(x,y), compared to the DFT Hessian (FD-of-analytical-gradient) on held-out geometries; and the success of Hessian-driven eigenvector-following transition-state (first-order saddle) optimization, DFT-verified at the endpoint

meta.conclusion: The hypothesis is REFUTED: on a controlled gene-regulatory network, a topology-agnostic neural-ODE cell simulator extrapolates to a structurally held-out (parameter-shifted) regime essentially identically to a mechanistic ODE given the correct regulatory topology (extrapolation-MSE ratio neural/mech = 0.999 +/- 0.002 across 4 seeds); both interpolate to ~1e-4 MSE but both collapse to ~0.116 MSE out-of-distribution. An oracle mechanistic model given the TRUE regime params reaches machine-precision zero (2.9e-15), isolating the failure to the unknown parameter shift; with 10 regime trajectories of fine-tuning both recover ~2 orders of magnitude and the mechanistic model becomes 1.3-2.8x better (ratio 1.86). So mechanism helps data-efficient regime adaptation, not zero-shot transfer; the bottleneck for a virtual cell is regime/parameter identification, not the learned-vs-mechanistic dichotomy that motivates the AIVC proposal.
meta.observable: extrapolation-MSE ratio = mean squared error of the neural-ODE trajectory prediction on out-of-distribution held-out states divided by that of the mechanistic ODE (both models trained on train-regime trajectories only); reported as mean+/-std over 4 GRN seeds. Secondary observable: per-model interpolation MSE and extrapolation MSE, and extrap_over_interp blow-up factor.

meta.conclusion: Direct sequence-identity matching of plate-community taxa against the complete RefSeq type-strain genome set (4,010 cultivable genera from 28,885 type-strain genomes) yields a proportion of cultivable TAXA (PCT_direct ≈ 48% at a mid dark-fraction, ratio 3.5x over the indirect proxy across the whole sweep) that is far above the ~1% cell-based PCC consensus (reproduced at PCC_direct ≈ 0.96%) and ~3.5x the indirect lab-workhorse-proxy estimate (PCT_indirect ≈ 14%); the model-independent named-genus audit (95% direct vs 27% indirect) corroborates the gap, supporting the hypothesis that indirect proxies underestimate cultivable-taxa coverage by roughly an order of magnitude relative to the cell-based consensus and ~3.5x relative to the classic allowlist proxy.
meta.observable: PCT (proportion of cultivable taxa) and PCC (proportion of cultivable cells), each computed under direct (sequence-identity-to-type-strain) vs indirect (classic-allowlist-proxy) cultivability decisions; plus the gap between them.

meta.conclusion: PENDING - awaiting completion of pretrain+SFT+PPO training and the three-way comparison. Preliminary infrastructure verification confirms the system computes all required observables; final conclusion will state whether PPO's joint yield exceeds SFT's, grounded in the actual generated-and-scored numbers.
meta.observable: Joint yield: fraction of generated molecules satisfying (valid SMILES AND QED >= 0.6 AND SA-score <= 5.0 AND novel vs training set), plus per-property breakdown (validity, mean QED, fraction QED>=0.6, mean SA, fraction SA<=5, novelty, internal diversity). This is the multi-property success-rate the TamGen tension names as unoptimized.

meta.conclusion: Hypothesis supported with moderate confidence: cheap stereoelectronic-proxy features reduce QM9 HOMO-LUMO gap test MAE from 0.2645 to 0.2247 eV (mean of 2 seeds), beating both the plain graph (−15.1%) and, by a smaller margin, an equal-dimension generic feature control (−3.4%); the se-vs-control gain (~0.008 eV) is consistent across both seeds and all 12 epochs but is comparable to seed-to-seed init noise (~0.016 eV), so SE-specific signal helps but its advantage over a generic feature budget is modest rather than decisive.
meta.observable: HOMO-LUMO gap test MAE (eV) — best-epoch-by-validation test MAE for each of the three conditions

meta.conclusion: Across 4 seeds the local coupled-learning rule (no global gradient) trained the 89-spring MNN to R^2=0.99993 on an 8D->8D vector task, retrained to a second task to R^2=0.99998, and recovered from pruning its 2 most-impactful springs (test error 3.2e-5 -> 1.9e-2 -> 3.4e-5 after continued local training), matching the exact adjoint-gradient baseline within noise (Task A 6.6e-5 vs 6.2e-5; both capabilities within ~6%). The hypothesis (a)-(d) is supported; the main caveat is overparameterization (the untrained control already achieves R^2~0.996), so the decisive evidence is the damage-recovery and task-switch tests rather than the raw R^2.
meta.observable: normalized test MSE = MSE / <|target output displacement|^2>  (i.e. 1 - R^2 of the vector output prediction); lower is better, 1.0 = no better than the mean output

meta.conclusion: A generative graph-attention model reconstructs completely destroyed fNIRS channels to r=0.93 in the no-clean-neighbor (island) case, beating the neighbor-mean baseline (0.89, which collapses to a global mean there) with very high significance (p=2.4e-130), supporting the hypothesis that generative recovery rescues the discarded-channel regime; however, when clean spatial neighbors exist, simple interpolation already reaches r~0.98 and the model adds little, so the model's value is specific to spatially-clustered or catastrophic damage rather than isolated single-channel loss.
meta.observable: Reconstruction Pearson correlation (r) of the destroyed channel's HbO/HbR timecourse vs ground truth, and functional-connectivity fidelity (Pearson r between the reconstructed and true 36x36 pairwise-correlation upper-triangles). Evaluated on a held-out test set of 3 subjects / 630 windows.

meta.conclusion: F- and O-termination of the Ti3C2 basal plane lower the interior vacancy formation energy relative to the bare surface (Ti2 by 0.46 eV under F, 0.68 eV under O; C by 6.90 eV under F), consistent with the hypothesis that passivation simultaneously makes the M-X sublattice more dissolution-prone and provides an atomistic mechanism for over-etching defects; the magnitude (esp. C, 6.90 eV) is likely inflated by the 18-atom cluster and should be read as directional, not quantitative.
meta.observable: Delta E_vac = E_vac(terminated) - E_vac(pristine) for interior Ti2 and C vacancy formation energies under F and O termination (eV); negative = termination makes the M/X sublattice vacancy more favorable (easier to dissolve)

meta.conclusion: On a benchmark calibrated to the public multi-sensor CowScreeningDB schema (43 cows, 11518 recordings, Sprecher 5-point locomotion scores, 100 Hz 13-channel IMU), a multiclass lameness-LEVEL deep-learning system IS achievable with non-trivial and reliable accuracy: the human-in-the-loop voting committee (3 deep nets + an interpretable gait-feature classifier, with abstention-based escalation of 11% of cases to human review) reaches 0.607 accuracy / 0.609 macro-F1, beating the 0.416 majority baseline by ~19 points and the raw deep net (0.561) by ~5 points on macro-F1; the interpretable features alone (0.607 macro-F1) are competitive with the full committee, supporting the claim that human-interpretable features materially help and that the human-in-loop abstention mechanism isolates genuinely uncertain cases rather than forcing unreliable guesses. HONEST CAVEAT (Stage F): because the original CowScreeningDB CSVs are gated behind a human-emailed license and were unobtainable, the signals come from a biomechanics-grounded generative surrogate calibrated to the published schema/counts, NOT the original recordings -- so the absolute numbers are a benchmark on the surrogate, not a measured performance on CowScreeningDB's real data; the contribution is the validated pipeline (multiclass DL + interpretable features + abstention voting) and its honest evaluation protocol, not a field-deployable accuracy claim.
meta.observable: Subject-level (cow-level) stratified 5-fold multiclass accuracy and macro-F1 for the Sprecher locomotion scores 1-5, comparing raw deep net vs interpretable-only vs deep+interpretable late fusion vs the full human-in-the-loop voting committee, against the majority-class and random baselines; plus escalation rate (% flagged for human review) and the per-class confusion matrix.

meta.conclusion: Honest leak-free persistence already achieves RMSE=1740 / R^2=0.989 on BTC daily, closely matching Helformer's own baselines (RMSE ~1150-1218, R^2 ~0.9944); Helformer's reported RMSE=7.75 / R^2=1.000 would require a 225x RMSE improvement and an exact R^2=1.000, which is only achievable if the test close leaks into the prediction, supporting the leaky-evaluation artifact hypothesis (pending deep-model confirmation).
meta.observable: test-set RMSE / R^2 of next-day close prediction (Helformer's own reported quantity: RMSE and R^2 on the BTC test close), and the leak-free directional proxy next-day-return R^2 / sign accuracy.

meta.conclusion: Lung-specific metastasis is well-described by a coevolutionary bistable system: a stable dormant and a stable outgrowth attractor coexist (H1 supported); the dormancy-to-outgrowth saddle-node threshold c* falls sharply as the tumor adaptive rate nu rises and is shifted by lung feedback (H2 supported); bidirectional tumor-lung feedback is load-bearing in the weak/interesting sense that decoupling shifts the threshold, freezes outgrowth burden against the tumor's own exosome output, and eliminates noise-driven reawakening entirely (0% escape vs 1-13% coupled) (H3 supported weakly, strong-collapse form refuted); lung-tropic exosome integrin coupling (alpha6beta4/alpha6beta1) produces the most immunosuppressive lung pre-metastatic niche, encoding organ tropism through PMN-readiness rather than escape probability.
meta.observable: saddle-node critical exosome coupling c* (coupling at which the stable high-burden outgrowth attractor annihilates), and mean first-passage time (MFPT) / reawakening probability from dormant to outgrowth basin under lung-immunosuppression noise; contrasted between coupled and lung-feedback-decoupled dynamics. Also outgrowth immunosuppression S_out and burden N_out versus coupling c.

meta.conclusion: A path-parametrized PINN whose physics loss is the energy-stationarity residual dU/dw-P=0, given a few branch-selection anchor points, traces the FULL folded equilibrium path of a von Mises shallow truss (snap-through load P_cr to 1.8%+/-1.5% over 3 seeds, second/post-critical limit to 2.0%+/-2.0%, post-critical branch reached in all seeds) and reads the critical load off the trained network automatically -- but the residual alone collapses to the trivial branch, so branch selection is essential; the headline hypothesis is supported with this caveat.
meta.observable: Snap-through (limit-point) critical load P_cr of the shallow truss equilibrium path P(w), and the full path RMS error against the closed-form P(w)=dU/dw. Auto-extracted from the PINN as the extremum of the learned P(t).

meta.conclusion: The Stage-A hypothesis is conditionally, not uniformly, supported. Under the symmetric-overhead assumption (SDL and its reference share the same per-experiment integration overhead h), AF is a ratio and overhead cancels, so realized AF_wall tracks AF_count (0.95-1.00x) and is governed by algorithmic quality, NOT overhead - refuting the hypothesis. BUT under asymmetric overhead, where the bespoke SDL carries higher per-experiment integration cost than the manual reference (the situation the barriers literature actually describes), AF_wall collapses: at h_SDL=15 vs h_ref=0.5, AF_wall=0.61 (the SDL LOSES on wall-clock despite winning on experiment count), and at h_SDL=30 it is 0.31. So whether overhead reduction beats algorithmic improvement for democratization hinges on whether SDL overhead is common-mode with the reference - i.e., on exactly the framework/standardization intervention the barriers literature advocates. The honest resolution: the field's experiment-count metrics survive wall-clock translation only when overhead is symmetric; the framework hypothesis holds in the realistic asymmetric regime that bespoke SDLs actually occupy.
meta.observable: wall-clock acceleration factor AF_wall = T_ref/T_AL (compared with experiment-count AF = n_ref/n_AL as defined in Adesiji et al. arXiv:2508.06642 Eq.2)

meta.conclusion: On real data from 17 cohorts, gut-microbiome PD classifiers are strongly study-specific: mean within-study AUC 0.725 collapses to 0.566 in cross-study transfer (a 0.159-AUC generalization gap, with 24% of transfer pairs worse than chance), and pooling multiple studies via leave-one-study-out recovers 54% of that gap (LOSO AUC 0.651) — reproducing and supporting the paper's claim that the diagnostic signal is real but only partially portable, and that multi-study training materially improves cross-population generalizability.
meta.observable: mean AUC (area under the ROC curve) for PD vs HC classification — reported separately for within-study, cross-study, and leave-one-study-out (LOSO) scenarios, exactly as in Romano et al. 2025

meta.conclusion: Explosive eruptions onto vegetated tropical terrain are net carbon SOURCES, not sinks: although the gross avoided-remineralization sink from SOC burial is comparable to magmatic CO2 (median ratio 1.7), the foregone NPP uptake from tephra-killed vegetation is ~4x larger, so the net burial perturbation is a source (~150 Tg CO2-eq for a Pinatubo-like event) that adds to magmatic CO2 rather than offsetting it; the consensus is upheld on the sign, and the burial term is non-negligible (gross ~ magmatic CO2) but only in the direction that makes eruptions larger net sources, with the sole exception of eruptions onto already-degraded low-biomass land.
meta.observable: net burial carbon perturbation / magmatic CO2 source (ratio_net) for a Pinatubo-like eruption, and the same ratio summed over a tropical arc per century

meta.conclusion: Diffusion does carry recoverable functional-state information: an end-to-end CNN+transformer reaches 93-94% accuracy and estimates the anomalous exponent at ~0.06-0.10 MAE. But the hypothesised >5pp accuracy advantage over the classical MSD-feature pipeline is NOT met (DL is +1.7pp standard, +1.7pp noisy, and ties a strong XGBoost baseline on short tracks), so the headline 'DL beats classical on functional-state classification' is only weakly supported. DL's genuine and robust win is on the underlying physics: it correctly recovers alpha for ergodicity-broken models (CTRW/ATTM/SBM) where the classical time-averaged MSD-slope estimate catastrophically fails (per-class alpha MAE 0.45-0.51 vs DL 0.04-0.09).
meta.observable: functional-state classification accuracy (held-out) and anomalous-exponent alpha mean absolute error (alpha MAE), reported as DL-vs-classical gap in percentage points

meta.conclusion: The open-source 3DcellScope does NOT let users plug in and benchmark arbitrary AI nuclei-segmentation networks: its nuclei layer is hard-coupled to a vendored StarDist (StarDist2D/StarDist3D only; the GUI offers three StarDist model-folder choices, not architectures), while its cell-surface and whole-organoid levels are non-AI classical watershed/thresholding — so the paper's 'plug-and-play / universal AI-powered' benchmarking claim is not realized by the released code without source modification.
meta.observable: nuclei-backend coupling — whether the segmentation pipeline exposes an architecture-agnostic adapter/strategy interface for nuclei segmentation or instead hard-calls StarDist3D/StarDist2D.predict_instances directly (the paper's own framing is a 'universal AI-powered', 'plug-and-play' pipeline that lets users 'plug in and benchmark arbitrary AI nuclei-segmentation models').

meta.conclusion: Independent first-principles computation (Pauli commutator-closure for X_exp, explicit dense gradient-operator partition for F_eff) is consistent with the trade-off: across HEA, SLPA, and commuting-generator ansatze up to n=6, every deep-limit (X_exp,F_eff) pair satisfies X_exp<=4^n/F_eff-F_eff and X_exp>=F_eff (10/10 structural cases), the SLPA with s independent stabilizers exactly saturates the upper bound (X_exp=4^n/2^s-2^s, F_eff=2^s at four (n,s) settings), and the universal HEA forces F_eff=1; however, the upper bound is a strictly asymptotic deep-circuit relation that is transiently violated at the finite depths I could compute (F_eff^(L) approaches its asymptote from above), so the bound's deep-limit universality is confirmed on a finite spanning sample and corroborated by, but not independently proven for, all deep QNNs.
meta.observable: X_exp (DLA dimension) and F_eff (mean simultaneously-measurable gradient components); trade-off bound X_exp <= 4^n/F_eff - F_eff

meta.conclusion: Against the hypothesis, adding a lambda=1.0 k-space data-consistency loss to an identical CNN did NOT significantly improve in-distribution accelerated MRI reconstruction (pooled NMSE gap -0.003, p=0.66) and did not reliably reduce the data-consistency residual — the physics term was underweighted (~4% of the image loss) and the predicted 'largest gap at small N, shrinking with N' pattern was not observed (PI was actually worse at N=8 and N=256). The only directional support is a small, non-significant out-of-distribution generalization advantage (pooled -0.017, p=0.24), pending a lambda-weighting sensitivity check.
meta.observable: Normalized mean squared error (NMSE = ||recon - gt||^2 / ||gt||^2) on held-out test set, with PSNR (fixed data range) and SSIM as secondary metrics and the data-consistency residual ||M.F(x_hat)-y||^2 as a physics-fidelity check

meta.conclusion: In a kinetic model of the tumor exosome-immune axis, exosome-level interventions (biogenesis inhibition or depletion) reverse the tumor-escape phenotype and restore effector control across a sharp, parameter-dependent dose threshold (~70% biogenesis block at baseline), with a downstream cargo-only block remaining partial — supporting exosomes as a high-leverage upstream therapeutic node, though the conclusion is model-derived from assumed (not patient-fitted) kinetic parameters and demonstrated only on the tumor side, so it is a mechanistic hypothesis with qualitative literature support rather than a quantitative prediction.
meta.observable: Effector-to-tumor ratio E/T at t=60 d (field term: effector immune control), with tumor_controlled = (T<10 and E>1); and the biogenesis-block fraction at which E/T crosses 1.0 (the escape/control threshold).

meta.conclusion: The measured Co/Mn/Zn impurity diffusivities in TiZrHfNbTa are quantitatively reproduced (within a factor of ~2, no free parameters) by a dissociative mechanism in which the interstitial site fraction f_int(T), computed from the independently measured solution-energy distributions, sets the diffusion channel weight; the larger local lattice distortion of TiZrHfNbV (independently confirmed by a radius-based strain variance sigma_eps ratio 1.36, close to the neutron/DFT delta ratio 1.55) correlates with greater diffusion enhancement, but a pure size-mismatch model underestimates the effect, supporting the paper's conclusion that both lattice distortion (electronic, not just size) and the dissociative interstitial mechanism — not sluggish vacancy diffusion — govern impurity diffusion in these BCC RHEAs.
meta.observable: Interstitial site fraction f_int(T) for Co/Mn/Zn in each alloy; the ratio D_Co/D_Zn (measured) vs f_int(Co)/f_int(Zn) (predicted) at 1073-1323 K; the local NN strain variance sigma_eps and its V/Ta ratio; the Co cross-over temperature Tcr between the two alloys.

meta.conclusion: The crystal structures themselves resolve the discrepancy: in the unmethylated-DNA (autoinhibited) state the CXXC domain forms a strong, Arg/Lys-mediated attractive interface with unmethylated CpG (computed CXXC-vs-DNA = -9685 kJ/mol, Coulomb -9565) - this is the structural basis of the high-affinity UMDNA binding seen in solution - while the catalytic MTase domain simultaneously binds the DNA backbone but holds the unmethylated target cytosine 18.2 A away from the catalytic Cys1229 (vs 2.81 A for the flipped hemimethylated base in 4DA4), and the CXXC-BAH1 linker is repulsive against DNA (+1181 kJ/mol) consistent with a steric occlusion plug; high-affinity binding and weak catalysis therefore coexist in one conformation rather than being contradictory.
meta.observable: Cytosine-C5 to catalytic-cysteine-SG distance (nm) in the UMDNA autoinhibited vs hemimethylated active crystal state, and domain-vs-DNA interaction energy (kJ/mol) partitioned across CXXC / BAH1 / BAH2 / catalytic-MTase.

meta.conclusion: PARTIAL REFUTATION: the first-principles framework predicts alpha-CD (not beta-CD) has the strongest naphthalene inclusion binding (-10.92 vs -8.70 kcal/mol), refuting the affinity half of the hypothesis; beta-CD selectivity for naphthalene over common interferents is modest (~2.5 kcal/mol mean). The recommendation therefore cannot rest on binding affinity alone — the SERS chemical-enhancement axis (in progress) must be weighed, and the gas-phase binding limitation noted.
meta.observable: Raman activity S_k (au) per normal mode of the analyte, and the SERS chemical enhancement ratio S_complexed / S_free for characteristic naphthalene Raman bands; plus inclusion binding energy dE_bind (grid-scan minimum over axial offset x in-plane rotation).

meta.conclusion: At reduced scale on real TCGA data, the multimodal model (UNI2-h histology + age/sex/stage) reproduces the PROGPATH claim that histology+clinical beats clinical-only on a multi-cancer internal held-out test (C-index 0.684 vs 0.664; 0.714 vs 0.691 over 5 seeds), and beats histology-only throughout; however the harder claim — that the multimodal gain GENERALIZES to unseen cancers — does NOT reproduce: in leave-one-cancer-type-out evaluation, clinical-only (0.639) outperforms multimodal (0.610) on average and in only 8/16 cancers, and histology-only collapses toward chance (0.550). The constructive part of the open question is supported; the generalization part is not, at this scale.
meta.observable: concordance index (C-index) for overall survival, computed (a) on internal held-out test and (b) as mean over leave-one-cancer-type-out folds, for multimodal vs histology-only vs clinical-only models

meta.conclusion: Forcing a single uniform weather-migration coefficient masks large opposing demographic responses: in a panel where weather is the dominant driver for every group but responses cancel in the aggregate, the uniform model reports a near-zero coefficient (0.024, R^2=8e-5) reproducing the literature's 'weather explains little', while the group-interacted model recovers the planted coefficients accurately and attributes 85.6x more variance to weather.
meta.observable: incremental McFadden pseudo-R^2 attributable to weather (over a region+year fixed-effects null), for the uniform-coefficient model vs. the group-interacted model; ratio of the two; and recovery of planted group-specific weather coefficients

meta.conclusion: Applied to the same 5,403 FNDDS foods, HPF and UPF overlap only moderately (Jaccard 0.52, Cohen's kappa 0.27 = only 'fair' agreement) and 25.5% of foods are flagged as 'addictive' by exactly one of the three terms, so the interchangeable use of these differently defined terms is an empirical confound — not merely semantic — that should be resolved before food addiction can become a reproducible construct.
meta.observable: Pairwise set-overlap between the three food classifications: Jaccard index and Cohen's kappa for (HPF vs UPF), (HPF vs highly processed), and (UPF vs highly processed); plus the fraction of foods flagged by exactly one construct.

meta.conclusion: My own cross-method x cross-modality computation does NOT support the Stage-A hypothesis that the bio-vs-batch trade-off is strong for diagonal RNA+ATAC and weak for vertical RNA+ADT; in fact, with discriminating metrics the trade-off is strongest for vertical RNA+ADT (rho=-0.83, p=0.042) and weakest for diagonal RNA+ATAC (rho=-0.38, ns) -- the reverse of the hypothesis -- while the paper-style composite (weakened by constant/floored batch metrics iLISI and GC) shows all three combos weakly negative and non-significant (rho ~ -0.21 to -0.26). The trade-off exists qualitatively (the single aggressive batch-corrector harmony_strong sacrifices bio for batch in every combo) but is not robustly modality-dependent in the direction predicted; confidence is moderate because the conclusion is sensitive to metric choice and rests on generated per-modality features with an extreme batch separation that floored iLISI/GC.
meta.observable: Spearman rank correlation (rho) between the composite biological-conservation score (mean of minmax-scaled cLISI, ARI_cellType, NMI_cellType, ASW_cellType, iASW) and the composite batch-correction score (mean of minmax-scaled ASW_batch, iLISI, GC), computed across integration methods separately per modality combination. The paper's own quantity names are cLISI, ARI_cellType, NMI_cellType, ASW_cellType, iASW, ASW_batch, iLISI, GC.

meta.conclusion: PDBbind v2020 / CASF-2016 is heavily redundant across the train/test boundary: 99.3% of test complexes share a UniProt protein with the training pool and 31% have an exact-duplicate ligand; removing shared proteins drops a transferable ligand-only model from Pearson R=0.72 to 0.60 (Ridge; RF: 0.70 to 0.54), so a substantial fraction of reported scoring power reflects memorizing recurring proteins and ligands rather than transferable structure-affinity learning, though a real residual signal (~R=0.55-0.60) survives even full de-duplication.
meta.observable: CASF-2016 'scoring power' = Pearson correlation R between predicted and experimental -logKd/Ki on the 285-complex core set (with Spearman rho and RMSE), reported as a function of the train/test split protocol.

meta.conclusion: The efficiency ceiling is set primarily by optical depth, not by the slow-light/finesse tradeoff: at the paper's 6 MHz multimode bandwidth, echo fidelity stays ~0.97 for every AFC finesse tested, so high finesse is NOT needed for bandwidth -- and absorption enhancement raising d_tilde from 0.97 to 2.6 lifts efficiency from 64% to 81% at moderate F_AFC=12 while letting the cavity stay broadband (bare finesse 13.6, linewidth 1.25 GHz >> 6 MHz). The cavity's multiplicative gain it supplies falls from ~37x to ~6.7x as OD rises, quantifying how the enhanced medium escapes dependence on a fragile high-finesse cavity. The open question is resolved: enhance optical depth (not finesse), keep the cavity impedance-matched and broadband.
meta.observable: storage-and-retrieval efficiency eta (echo energy / input energy) and the echo-pulse fidelity (|<echo|input>|^2 / (||echo||^2 ||input||^2)) as a proxy for slow-light distortion / multimode bandwidth

meta.conclusion: A bulk-phase resistance model with independently measured parameters reproduces observed SO2 uptake coefficients to within an order of magnitude across the droplet-size/pH space, and the apparent 'excess' uptake in short-exposure experiments is reproduced by transient bulk depletion (gamma decaying from the gas+accommodation limit toward steady state, up to ~6x at low pH) without invoking a distinct interfacial reaction; bulk-phase processes therefore dominate, though the result hinges on alpha ~ 0.1 and k_hyd >= 1e4 s^-1, and cannot exclude a modest interfacial contribution within the residual.
meta.observable: SO2 reactive uptake coefficient gamma (dimensionless fraction of gas-droplet collisions leading to net uptake), at steady state and as a transient gamma(t).

meta.conclusion: The competing CT-quenching channel is ~31x more sensitive to nitroarene identity than E_T (dG_RQ range 10.7 eV vs E_T range 0.34 eV; Pearson EA vs dG_RQ = -0.999), so the E_T-matching criterion alone genuinely cannot explain reactivity differences - but under realistic contact exciplex stabilization (1-3 eV) my Marcus/Dexter model keeps the entire E_T-matched family on the isomerizing side (f_iso=1.0), only splitting at an unphysically large Delta_CT~3.5 eV; the hypothesis is therefore supported as a sensitivity-rank-ordering explanation but only weakly supported as the cause of regime-level quenching for cinnamate specifically.
meta.observable: spread (range) of the CT-competition driving force dG_RQ across the family, compared with the spread of E_T; and the splitting threshold of the isomerization fraction f_iso = k_TTET/(k_TTET+k_CT) as a function of contact-CT stabilization Delta_CT

meta.conclusion: A K48-anchored avidity kinetic model reproduces the tetraubiquitin threshold (half-maximal apparent degradation at n~3.8) and predicts that, if K11 chains are more open than K48 as their diubiquitin structure suggests, K11 is a measurably weaker proteasomal degradation signal specifically at short chains (n=2-4, up to ~3-fold lower k_deg_app), so proteasome-level linkage discrimination is plausible and concentrates at the very chain lengths the tetra threshold occupies; H0 (no linkage discrimination) is refuted conditionally on the open-K11 premise being realized in vivo.
meta.observable: apparent first-order degradation rate constant k_deg_app(n,L) (the proteasome-kinetics analog of k_cat/K_m), and the linkage-discrimination metric D = max_n |log2( k_deg_app(n,K11) / k_deg_app(n,K48) )|

meta.conclusion: A deterministic, scale-covariant diagnostic linking seismic moment to permeability exists: V_dil = (tan phi/G) * SigmaM0 (verified to machine precision, ~1e-16), yielding k_after/k_before = (1 + (tan phi/G)(SigmaM0/V)(L/b0))^3; the relation is exactly scale-invariant across cm-to-sub-km only when fracture aperture scales self-similarly with spacing, and degrades gracefully (modest scale dependence, 3.4x spread for h=0.5) for the realistic sub-self-similar aperture-length scaling of natural joints.
meta.observable: Relative permeability enhancement k_after/k_before = (1 + (tan(phi)/G) * (SigmaM0/V) * (L/b0))^3, and its determinism kernel the cumulative seismic moment SigmaM0 = sum of individual event moments M0,e.

meta.conclusion: Under the physically-grounded poroelastic loading regime (nucleus pressure rise driving endplate-dominated efflux), the outer-annulus lymphatic route carries only ~3-4% of total disc fluid efflux in healthy discs and stays below 10% even under degeneration and active lymphatic pumping — supporting the hypothesis that lymphatics are quantitatively negligible as a DRAINAGE route under typical conditions; however, the hypothesis is falsified in the severe-endplate-degeneration regime (low-end CEP permeability, AF/CEP~15x) where phi_L rises to ~26%, and the result is contingent on the source distribution (unphysical annulus-generated fluid gives a 36% upper bound), so the honest verdict is that lymphatics are drainage-minor in healthy/typical discs but can become a load-bearing drainage route when the endplate is severely compromised.
meta.observable: lymphatic drainage fraction phi_L = Q_lymphatic / (Q_endplate + Q_lymphatic) integrated over the disc boundaries under diurnal poroelastic loading (computed at steady state and confirmed by transient diurnal run)

meta.conclusion: At daily timescale the hypothesis is REFUTED: dGPP/dCF is negative at virtually all sites (clouds suppress GPP via light) and becomes MORE negative, not less, in wetter sites (arid -0.26 vs humid -0.41 weighted standardized slope), with no zero-crossing near HI=1 (extrapolated crossover HI=-4.4, outside the data). However, at monthly timescale the gradient moves toward the predicted direction-arid sites become substantially less negative (mean -0.14, 30% positive) while humid sites remain more negative (-0.23, 14% positive)-consistent with a delayed water channel that the instantaneous daily light-loss channel masks but does not produce a clean sign reversal in this site-level FLUXNET sample.
meta.observable: dGPP/dCF: standardized partial regression slope of deseasonalized daily (and monthly) GPP anomaly on cloud-cover anomaly per FLUXNET site, in units of z-scored GPP per z-scored CF (dimensionless slope).

meta.conclusion: Bacterial TLPs and metazoan Teneurin-2 share a quantitatively conserved core fold — TM-align superposes 976 residues at 3.76 Å Cα RMSD with TM-score 0.705, well above the 0.5 same-fold threshold and ~3–10× above unrelated-protein controls (TM 0.12–0.32) and a scrambled-coordinate null (TM 0.06–0.08) — confirming a shared extended YD-repeat barrel bridging bacterial accessory toxin and metazoan neuronal receptor, while the C-terminal toxin/accessory modules do not share a conserved fold (TM 0.216), consistent with their role as swappable accessory modules repurposed as the metazoan TCAP/neuropeptide-like domain.
meta.observable: TM-score (length-normalized structural similarity, 0–1) and Cα RMSD over the TM-align core, with aligned-length and sequence identity, contrasted against negative/null controls.

meta.conclusion: Standard empirical velocity-porosity models only weakly predict reservoir velocities in the Missakeswal mixed carbonate-Cambrian-sand setting: carbonate Vp predictions capture ~70% of variance (R2 up to 0.71) but only ~56-63% of samples fall within a generous +/-0.30 km/s tolerance because pore-type diversity dominates over porosity, and Cambrian sandstone velocities are systematically under-predicted (multiple models yield negative R2; <36% within a tight +/-0.15 km/s) because the Han/Tosaya clay-rich lab calibrations do not match the cleaner, more rigid Cambrian frame — so the assumed applicability of these models for reservoir-quality and saturation prediction here is NOT supported.
meta.observable: P-wave (Vp) and S-wave (Vs) velocity prediction error of each empirical model against the physically-grounded truth, quantified as RMSE (km/s), mean bias, R^2, and within-tolerance fraction.

meta.conclusion: On a strong in-distribution fracture classifier (val AUROC 0.93), discrimination collapsed by 25-29% under anatomy and view-angle shifts (AUROC 0.87->0.62 hand, 0.87->0.66 oblique), calibration degraded dramatically under prevalence shift (ECE 0.12->0.65 on hip), and temperature scaling fit in-domain was useless (T=1.005, ECE unchanged on all OOD sets) because the OOD failure is distributional, not overconfidence - supporting the paper's stated translation gap.
meta.observable: AUROC drop (in-distribution vs out-of-distribution), Expected Calibration Error (ECE, 10 equal-width bins), Brier score, and negative log-likelihood (NLL) per evaluation set, before and after temperature scaling.

meta.conclusion: Across 200 simulated single-cell realizations, resolving cell-cell communication at the specific transcription-factor node (Method C) ranked true EMT-driver ligands with precision@3 = 0.985 and NEVER miscredited the coarse-label confounder BMP4, whereas the LR-only method (precision@3 = 0.000, miscredited BMP4 on 100% of seeds) and the coarse-pathway downstream method (precision@3 = 0.650, miscredited BMP4 on 98.5% of seeds) were systematically fooled by high decoy expression and family-label sharing; adding an LLM-style literature prior on top of the coarse method did not close the gap (0.667, BMP4 still miscredited 97%), indicating the convergence-resolution step itself — not the LLM contextualization layer — carries the mechanistic value, supporting the hypothesis, though on synthetic data with a hand-curated pathway KB.
meta.observable: precision@3 (fraction of top-3 ranked ligands that are true EMT drivers) and BMP4 miscrediting rate (fraction of seeds where the coarse-label confounder BMP4 appears in the top-3), across 200 simulated single-cell realizations

meta.conclusion: Hypothesis refuted within the studied cohort: a learned autoencoder-k-NN patient-similarity representation did NOT match the supervised gradient-boosting LOS baseline (MAE 1.48 d vs 1.40 d; better in 0% of bootstraps), added nothing over raw k-NN, and produced neighbourhoods at chance clinical coherence (label purity 0.81 vs 0.84 chance; STAT silhouette ~0); in paediatric cardiology a directly supervised model dominates, and similarity-based LOS retrieval offers no advantage here. Generalization to real paediatric-cardiology EHRs is unproven given the synthetic, literature-calibrated cohort.
meta.observable: length-of-stay (LOS) prediction mean absolute error in days (MAE, days), with prolonged-LOS AUROC, neighbour label-purity, and embedding silhouette as coherence observables

meta.conclusion: Preliminary: pending computation. Real ISD air-temperature pipeline verified for NYC cluster (Central Park/JFK/LaGuardia urban vs Sandy Hook rural, 2023, hourly T_a parsed and sanity-checked).
meta.observable: UHI_a (canopy air-temperature urban heat island, deg C) computed from ISD, and the bias |UHI_s - UHI_a| when T_s is used as a proxy for T_a; secondarily the R^2 of a Ts->Ta transfer model versus a Ts-only proxy.

meta.conclusion: Low-order truncated PN (Newtonian) differs dramatically from 2PN TaylorF2 in the LISA band for MBHB (e.g., match ~0.078 for 1e6 Msun equal-mass), indicating leading-order PN alone is insufficient for LISA waveform fidelity.
meta.observable: noise-weighted match between Newtonian (0PN) and 2PN restricted TaylorF2 waveforms over LISA band (dimensionless)

meta.conclusion: Within a well-mixed cytosolic buffered model using literature-informed buffer parameters, modest ZIP4 overexpression (≤10x) increases free cytosolic Zn2+ only into the sub-nanomolar range; reaching micromolar concentrations (required to directly activate MTF-1 in cell assays) requires extreme influx increases (≈1000-fold) or substantial reduction/saturation of buffer capacity. Therefore, ZIP4-driven oncogenic signaling is unlikely to result solely from a homogeneous rise of cytosolic free Zn2+ sufficient to activate MTF-1; other mechanisms (local microdomains, MT release via ROS, or signaling pathways downstream of ZIP4) are implicated.
meta.observable: steady-state cytosolic free Zn2+ concentration `Z_free` (M)

meta.conclusion: Representative large bubbles of radius ~2 mm have terminal rise speeds ~0.52 m/s; literature-reported Marangoni-driven melt-pool velocities (0.3–1.0+ m/s) are in the same range, supporting that recirculating melt flow can overcome buoyancy and stably entrain mm-scale bubbles in DED melt pools.
meta.observable: terminal_rise_velocity_of_bubble (U_t, m/s) as function of bubble radius (mm)

meta.conclusion: Preliminary pooled estimate for parental digital use indicates a small-to-moderate positive association with preschoolers' prolonged digital use (pooled r≈0.31), but the 95% CI spans zero and heterogeneity is large; evidence is suggestive but not conclusive.
meta.observable: Pearson correlation (r) between parental factor (here: parental digital use) and preschoolers' daily screen time / odds of exceeding recommended 1 h/day, converted to r when necessary.

meta.conclusion: Station-based precipitation predictability metrics (lag-1 autocorrelation and previous-day AUC) are modestly lower in the sampled African stations than the sampled European stations, consistent with the hypothesis that lower precipitation predictability contributes to poorer short-term flood forecast skill in Africa.
meta.observable: lag-1 autocorrelation of daily precipitation anomalies; AUC of previous-day predictor for daily precipitation >95th percentile

meta.conclusion: Simulated ensembles with log-uniform switching times spanning ~8 decades produce an almost perfectly linear mapping (R^2=0.9996) between log10(pulse width) and ensemble mean conductance; narrower or linear tau distributions reduce linearity.
meta.observable: ensemble_mean_fraction_switched (unitless; proxy for normalized conductance/voltage)

meta.conclusion: For the tested geometry (0.5 km strand spacing, 60 km along-strike, 10 km downdip) and parameters, splitting slip onto three closely spaced strands reduces mean Coulomb stress by ~978 Pa (≈0.001 MPa) and produces only minor changes in immediate seismicity-rate metrics (given plausible Aσ values), suggesting multifaulting at this scale modestly broadens but does not qualitatively change short-term static stress triggering patterns.
meta.observable: Mean Coulomb stress change on the receiver interface (ΔCFF, Pa) and derived mean seismicity-rate ratio R = mean(exp(ΔCFF/(Aσ))).

meta.conclusion: In this simulated cohort, naive Kaplan–Meier/Cox-style approaches that censor competing non-CVD death substantially overpredict 10-year CVD risk in older adults (age 75–89) and in people with severe comorbidity; competing-risk (CIF) methods and inclusion of predictors of non-CVD death materially reduce predicted risks.
meta.observable: 10-year cumulative incidence (probability) of first CVD event (CIF) and corresponding naive 1-KM estimate

meta.conclusion: Under the Park-model finite-rate oxidation assumptions and assuming ~1% O2 dissociation at T=2500 K, p=1000 Pa, graphite recession is ~5.3e-7 m/s (≈1.9 mm/h); this shows literature-rate predictions imply non-negligible ablation and strong sensitivity to dissociation fraction.
meta.observable: graphite surface recession rate (m/s)

meta.conclusion: In this initial analysis of 6 samples, MES-like spots showed significantly higher macrophage scores in 1 samples (out of 4) — limited but suggestive evidence for the hypothesis
meta.observable: mean Macrophage module score in spots dominated by MES state (log1p CPM average)

meta.conclusion: In this simulation, annotation-informed modeling on the higher-density panel improved within-ancestry R^2 modestly and improved cross-ancestry transfer compared to the low-density panel, consistent with the hypothesis (see report for caveats).
meta.observable: Prediction R^2 on held-out test sets (within-ancestry and cross-ancestry)

meta.conclusion: Preliminary: hybrid (LLM+OPSIN fallback) shows higher accuracy than LLM-alone on this 30-name sample
meta.observable: fraction of test names for which output molecule equals OPSIN molecule (accuracy)

meta.conclusion: Based on current evidence and the (limited) computations performed here, C13 is best described as an open-shell triplet with a kinked (bond-length-alternated) geometry; C26 is consistent with a closed-shell even ring. This conclusion is primarily supported by high-level literature calculations and partially by our SCF behavior, though our in-session DFT optimizations were inconclusive.
meta.observable: Singlet–triplet energy gap ΔE(S–T) (kcal mol^-1) and bond-length alternation metrics (mean, std, min, max bond lengths in Angstrom)

meta.conclusion: In these single-sample, diploid, heterozygous simulations with moderate depth (200) and purity (0.8), a Dirichlet-process-style BayesianGaussianMixture recovered clone assignments substantially more accurately for 3-clone mixtures than fixed-K or BIC-selected GMMs; advantage shrinks for 2 clones and diminishes as complexity (4 clones) increases.
meta.observable: assignment_accuracy (fraction of mutations assigned to correct true clone after optimal label matching)

meta.conclusion: Hypothesis supported in the simulated cohort.
meta.observable: cross-validated macro F1 score for 4-way classification

meta.conclusion: Preliminary evidence from a 2000-site subset of the CPTAC GBM phosphoproteome shows a modest set of phosphosites (38 sites at raw p<0.01) differing between EGFR-mutant and wildtype tumors, consistent with the hypothesis that EGFR alteration impacts downstream phosphorylation patterns; however this is an incomplete analysis (subset) and requires full-cohort, multiple-testing-corrected validation.
meta.observable: number_of_phosphosites_with_raw_p<0.01 (in the tested subset)

meta.conclusion: On this synthetic pathology-like task, a model trained on one tissue shows near-chance zero-shot performance (AUC=0.5) on a different tissue, but a small number of target labels (10–50) suffice to reach near-perfect AUC; transfer from the source gives modest benefit at 10-shot and both approaches reach near-perfect performance by 50-shot.
meta.observable: ROC AUC on held-out target test set (target_test)

meta.conclusion: In this coarse-grained two-angle chain model, enforcing a symmetric small entry-exit angle (on-dyad) yields a strongly compacted 12-mer (mean Rg ~10.17 nm) compared with the no‑H1 open case (mean Rg ~22.79 nm); the off‑dyad asymmetric constraint produces a similar Rg (~10.48 nm) to on‑dyad in this model, suggesting both constrained entry‑exit geometries can compact arrays to comparable extents in this approximation.
meta.observable: Radius of gyration (Rg) of the 12-nucleosome array (nm)

meta.conclusion: On this synthetic benchmark TS2Vec (as used here) did not outperform the LSTM autoencoder; the LSTM-AE achieved F1=0.686 while TS2Vec failed or produced no positive signal.
meta.observable: point-level F1 (binary anomaly detection per timestamp)

meta.conclusion: Preliminary: median literature values in this small sample show single-crystal NMC retains more capacity than polycrystalline NMC in the ~200–600 cycle window under reported protocols, but data are heterogeneous and protocols differ.
meta.observable: Capacity retention (%) after N cycles (N ≈200–300 where available)

meta.conclusion: On this Müller–Brown test, an ML potential trained only on energies and forces failed to reproduce the negative curvature of the saddle: the true Hessian had eigenvalues [-750.86, 490.24] while the model produced [~42.37, ~51.37] (both positive). This suggests energies+forces alone may be insufficient to guarantee correct Hessian signs/magnitudes for transition-state curvature in general.
meta.observable: Hessian matrix (2x2) evaluated at the PES saddle point

meta.conclusion: On these synthetic multi-scale compartmental systems up to 200 state dimensions, a small MLP surrogate offered modest reduction in one-step normalized error (~11.6% at S=40) and inference time was not consistently faster than a compiled linear Euler baseline; results do not yet support the stronger claim that learned surrogates reliably and cheaply replace mechanistic simulators at these scales.
meta.observable: one-step normalized root-mean-squared error (nRMSE) for predicting next state, and per-sample inference time (s).

meta.conclusion: Pilot sampling shows a very low exact-match rate (2/200 = 1%), refuting the hypothesis that >=20% of common environmental OTUs have exact matches to sequences in rrnDB (cultured isolate proxy).
meta.observable: PCT_exact_match: fraction of environmental OTUs with an exact V4-region substring present in sampled rrnDB sequences

meta.conclusion: Adding approximate stereoelectronic features produced modest but consistent improvements in predictive performance (lower RMSE, higher R^2) for HOMO energy and dipole moment on a 5k-sample QM9 subset using RandomForest models.
meta.observable: Test-set RMSE and R^2 for predicted HOMO energy (eV) and dipole moment (Debye).

meta.conclusion: A simple 3x3 spring lattice trained with a two-phase local equilibrium-prop-like rule achieved final RMSE ~0.688 on the synthetic 2->4 mapping, demonstrating that in-situ local learning can reduce task error in this setting (evidence is preliminary and limited in scale).
meta.observable: RMSE_output_displacement (same units as node coordinates)

meta.conclusion: On the synthetic dataset, the conv denoising autoencoder reduced masked-channel MSE to ~6.7e-4 (normalized units) but yielded mean Pearson r ~0.0; this partially falsifies the hypothesis as amplitude error was small but temporal correlation criterion (r>0.5) failed.
meta.observable: test_masked_mse (mean MSE computed only on corrupted channels, in normalized z-score units) and test_masked_pearson (mean Pearson r over reconstructed corrupted channels)

meta.conclusion: On a synthetic corpus that simulates clinician SUD severity wording, a TF-IDF + logistic regression classifier substantially outperforms a simple rule-based extractor (F1_macro 0.773 vs 0.667). Attempts to run a zero-shot LLM (Flan-T5) here were unsuccessful due to environment/download constraints, so the hypothesis about LLM superiority remains untested empirically in this run.
meta.observable: classification F1 (macro) and accuracy for mapping a note to one of the labels {none,in_remission,mild,moderate,severe}

meta.conclusion: For the three tested models, sub-Chandrasekhar detonation yields (Mn/Fe ~8.8e-5, Ni/Fe ~5.5e-3) are far below the observed ranges for SNR 3C 397 (Mn/Fe~0.018–0.033, Ni/Fe~0.11–0.24), while near-Chandrasekhar DDT models produce higher Mn/Fe and Ni/Fe but still underpredict the highest observed Ni/Fe. This supports the hypothesis that sub-Chandrasekhar models (as sampled) cannot account for the high neutronized iron-group ratios observed in some SNRs.
meta.observable: Mn/Fe and Ni/Fe mass ratios in the final (stable) ejecta — computed as mass(Mn_final)/mass(Fe_final) and mass(Ni_final)/mass(Fe_final)

meta.conclusion: Under the simplified impulse-scaling + Poisson detectability assumptions, cold, nearby, dense streams (GD-1-like) could in principle detect subhalos down to a few 10^5 M_sun; more distant, broader or sparser streams need masses of order 10^6–10^8 M_sun.
meta.observable: Minimum detectable subhalo mass M_min (M_sun) required to produce a gap meeting the SNR and resolution criteria

meta.conclusion: In this synthetic test, the smooth integrable (RBF-spline) transcription-rate parameterization recovered alpha(t) and u/s trajectories far more accurately than the single-switch stepwise model (order-of-magnitude lower MSEs).
meta.observable: Mean squared error (MSE) of recovered transcription rate alpha(t) over the time grid; MSE of reconstructed unspliced (u) and spliced (s) trajectories compared to ground truth (time-resolved ODE solution).

meta.conclusion: On this publicly-available feature matrix (AllCowsDataX) with synthetic 3-class labels derived from gait statistics, adding the chosen set of human-interpretable features and a simulated human-in-the-loop vote did not improve multiclass accuracy vs. a PCA-based MLP on raw features (baseline ~0.514 vs combined ~0.447; human-in-loop ~0.462).
meta.observable: 5-fold cross-validated multiclass accuracy (3 classes)

meta.conclusion: On the synthetic series and quick heuristic/mini-experiment run, the decomposition+heuristics produced much worse RMSE than simple persistence; hypothesis is falsified in this setup (evidence weak and method limited).
meta.observable: 1-day-ahead RMSE of predicted Close price (USD) on the held-out test set

meta.conclusion: Simulation shows a nonlinear, threshold-like increase in metastatic establishment probability with niche strength; S≈0.3–0.4 separates low vs high establishment probability under these model assumptions.
meta.observable: P_metastasis(T=200): probability a seeded DTC population produces >=50 cells by 200 time-steps

meta.conclusion: On a restricted domain around the critical region, a supervised NN reproduces critical points within ~2% in displacement and ~0.1% in load; physics-only PINN over the full domain failed without stronger data or normalization, so the hypothesis is partially supported but requires careful data/normalization choices.
meta.observable: Critical point locations (w, lambda) where dλ/dw=0 and their percent error vs analytic

meta.conclusion: Under the model and parameters used, halving integration overhead (S:0.0 -> 0.5) yields an ~18.8% reduction in mean cycle time and ~23.1% increase in throughput — short of the hypothesis thresholds — so the hypothesis (>=20% and >=30%) is not supported by this model.
meta.observable: mean_cycle_time_hours

meta.conclusion: Pooled cross-validated performance is good (AUROC~0.77) but cross-study portability is variable: LOSO mean AUROC ~0.698 (median ~0.709), indicating modest generalizability and substantial study-to-study heterogeneity.
meta.observable: Area under ROC curve (AUROC) measured on held-out test sets: pooled stratified 5-fold and LOSO per-study AUROC

meta.conclusion: Under conservative, spatially-uniform assumptions (V_magma=2.6 km^3; deposit mean thickness approximated by burial threshold = 0.1 m), tephra burial of SOC (≈1.83 Tg C) does not offset magmatic C emissions (≈7.09 Tg C): this eruption remains a net C source.
meta.observable: Total mass of SOC buried by tephra from a single eruption (Tg C), and total magmatic carbon emitted by the eruption (Tg C)

meta.conclusion: In synthetic, idealized trajectories diffusion-derived features allowed perfect separation of four motion classes; under added localization noise and shorter tracks, accuracy decreased (0.895→0.8) but remained well above chance, indicating diffusion features can carry functionally-relevant signal in controlled settings, though real experiments will be harder.
meta.observable: classification_accuracy_on_test_set

meta.conclusion: Preliminary result: conservative instruction did NOT reduce average clinical-severity score on this 5-note synthetic corpus (avg 21.0 -> 21.6). The result is limited by small synthetic dataset and heuristic NLI/omission scoring.
meta.observable: average_clinical_severity_score_per_note

meta.conclusion: A minimal integrated pipeline can be assembled and produces usable multi-level outputs; on the synthetic test, a classical watershed baseline achieved mean instance Dice ~0.783. Plugging in an off-the-shelf Cellpose 3D model was attempted but encountered configuration/download issues during this run, so fully automated benchmarking of multiple AI models on a standard laptop requires handling model downloads and 3D parameterization (feasible but nontrivial).
meta.observable: mean_instance_dice_nuclei

meta.conclusion: Preliminary numerical evidence (small circuits, 2--3 qubits) shows a negative Pearson correlation (r≈-0.72) between DLA dimension and fraction of parameters whose gradient operators can be measured simultaneously, suggesting a trade-off; evidence is limited and not definitive.
meta.observable: fraction_of_parameters_measurable_simultaneously (max commuting subset size / total parameters); and DLA dimension (rank in Pauli basis)

meta.conclusion: Preliminary result (small synthetic test) shows the physics-informed loss decreased PSNR by ~2.79 dB at n=8 (contrary to the hypothesis). This is an early, low-confidence finding and may reflect hyperparameter/training regime choices rather than a general failure of physics-informed approaches.
meta.observable: mean test PSNR (dB) on held-out set of 100 phantoms

meta.conclusion: Physiologic plasma exosome concentrations (10^8–10^11 particles/mL) can plausibly achieve 50% PD-1 occupancy only when individual exosomes present tens-to-thousands of PD-L1 molecules and/or effective affinity/avidity is substantially higher (KD in high-nM to low-nM); if PD-L1 copies per exosome are very low (≈4–6) and PD-1/PD-L1 KD is micromolar, physiologic concentrations are insufficient—so exosome-mediated suppression is plausible but parameter-dependent.
meta.observable: P50_particles_per_mL (particles/mL at which PD-L1 concentration equals KD leading to 50% PD-1 occupancy)

meta.conclusion: In the crystallographic binding poses, the DNMT1 catalytic domain buries substantially more surface area on hemimethylated DNA (approx 127 A^2) than on unmethylated DNA (approx 15 A^2); this structural difference predicts substantially weaker binding of the catalytic domain to the unmethylated DNA pose, consistent with the idea that solution high-affinity binding to unmethylated DNA must involve alternative modes or additional domains.
meta.observable: Buried surface area (BSA) at the protein-DNA interface (A^2); derived DeltaG (kcal/mol) and Kd (M) estimates from BSA.

meta.conclusion: All three tested receptors produce very similar predicted changes in isotropic polarizability upon binding benzene (Δα_iso ≈ -28 a.u.), so this simple polarizability-change proxy does not distinguish a clear winner for SERS chemical enhancement among these candidates under the tested geometry and level of theory.
meta.observable: delta_iso_polarizability (α_iso, complex - receptor) in atomic units

meta.conclusion: In this 1,998-patient pancancer subset, a unified model combining histomic features with simple clinical covariates produced a small improvement in median-split survival AUROC (mean AUROC ~0.596) over either modality alone, but gains are modest and uncertain.
meta.observable: AUROC for median-split overall survival (short <= median OS days vs long > median), evaluated by 5-fold CV

meta.conclusion: In this simulation, pooled regressions produce a modest/ambiguous temperature coefficient (mean pooled beta ≈ 0.103) while subgroup analyses show divergent and larger subgroup sensitivities (high-edu ≈ 0.175, low-edu ≈ 0.030); adding an interaction term increases R^2 roughly two-fold, supporting the hypothesis that demographic heterogeneity can mask stronger subgroup climate–migration relationships.
meta.observable: Estimated temperature coefficient on aggregate migration rate (OLS beta for temperature) and R-squared; subgroup-specific temperature coefficients and R-squared; interaction coefficient (T * share_high).

meta.conclusion: Preliminary: B3LYP (without explicit dispersion correction) does not reliably reproduce the negative CCSD(T) binding energies for dispersion-dominated ligand-pocket motifs; dispersion-aware functionals are required. Evidence here is limited and partial due to incomplete CCSD(T) runs.
meta.observable: Interaction energy (kcal/mol) = E(dimer) - E(monomerA) - E(monomerB)

meta.conclusion: In GroceryDB (n=25,957 items with complete nutrients), ~89% of items meeting Fazzino hyper-palatable criteria are also classified as ultra-processed by FoodProX (f_FPro_class==3), indicating high but not perfect overlap; the three terms are overlapping but not interchangeable.
meta.observable: fraction of HPF items that are classified as UPF in GroceryDB

meta.conclusion: On the PBMC CITE-seq subset and marker-based labels tested here, totalVI yields slightly higher classification accuracy and similar or slightly better silhouette than concatenation+PCA, and both outperform CCA.
meta.observable: 5-fold cross-validated classification accuracy (KNN) on marker-gene-derived cell-type labels; secondary observable: silhouette score of embedding by labels.

meta.conclusion: On this ligand-only baseline, test Pearson R falls from ~0.61 (random-like split) to ~0.47 (LP-PDBBind split) — an absolute drop of ~0.14 — indicating that standard splits in PDBbind inflate apparent generalization.
meta.observable: Pearson correlation coefficient (Pearson r) between predicted and experimental pKd on held-out test set

meta.conclusion: For representative AFC parameters (Δ=1 MHz, d_peak≈0.2, F≈30), intracavity slow-light delays are significant but substantially smaller than the AFC rephasing time (τ_g ≈0.13 μs versus t_echo=1 μs). Only for much higher finesse or much larger per-tooth optical depth (F≫100 or d_peak ≳1) does τ_g approach or exceed t_echo, indicating slow-light dispersion can limit bandwidth/multimode capacity in these extreme regimes.
meta.observable: max_group_delay_within_comb (τ_g_max) — maximum group delay inside the comb spectral window (units: seconds)

meta.conclusion: Under the modeled conditions and parameters (kb=1.7e7 s^-1, ks=9.7e5 s^-1, H=2.0 M/atm, D~1.8e-9 m^2/s), bulk hydrolysis accounts for >99% of SO2 reactive uptake for droplets ~1 μm, with interfacial processes contributing ~0.7%.
meta.observable: Reactive uptake coefficient γ (dimensionless) and interfacial fraction defined as 1 - γ_bulkonly/γ

meta.conclusion: Preliminary calculations show a methyl cinnamate vertical T1 ≈ 2.12 eV (delta-SCF, HF-level); initial data and literature suggest that differences in nitroarene T1 electronic configuration/localization (nπ* vs ππ*) — not only E_T — can explain differing EnT reactivity, but my computed numbers are method-limited and thus only support this hypothesis qualitatively.
meta.observable: vertical triplet energy E_T (defined as E_trip - E_sing, in eV) computed by delta-SCF; also Mulliken atomic spin populations on the triplet state

meta.conclusion: Under the in vitro–like parameter set used (low proteasome concentration, moderate ubiquitin ligation and modest DUB activity), substrates typically accumulate long K48 chains before being degraded (mean ~15 Ubs); thus the commonly-cited minimal signal of Ub4 is not a hard limit but an emergent property dependent on kinetic parameters.
meta.observable: chain_length_at_degradation (integer); also mean_chain_length and fraction_degraded_with_chain_>=_4

meta.conclusion: Under a simple single-fracture shear-dilation + cubic-law model, cumulative seismic moment maps to permeability increases extremely nonlinearly (exponent ~19 for the tested parameters), contradicting the original moderate-scaling hypothesis (Δk/k ∝ M0^{2/3}).
meta.observable: relative permeability change k_rel = (k - k0)/k0 where k ~ (hydraulic_aperture)^3, reported as a function of cumulative seismic moment M0_cum (N·m)

meta.conclusion: Optical losses due to finite absorber thickness, front-surface reflection and parasitic absorption can account for ~2.7–4.8 mA/cm^2 loss versus an idealized 100% EQE case (depending on bandgap); combined with bandgap choice and spectrum differences, these optical effects plausibly explain most of the observed J_sc deficit around 26 mA/cm^2.
meta.observable: J_sc (short-circuit current density, mA/cm^2)

meta.conclusion: Across the curated literature, lymphatic structures are repeatedly reported in degenerated or herniated intervertebral discs and in peridiscal/peri-vertebral tissues, but evidence for stable, functional lymphatics inside the healthy adult disc proper remains weak; the hypothesis is provisionally supported.
meta.observable: Study-level reported presence of lymphatic structures in IVD samples (binary: reported present vs absent).

meta.conclusion: For representative observed cell concentrations (≈2.9×10^4 cells mL^-1) and measured stoichiometry, nanomolar DIP concentrations in the tens of nM — especially when combined with an appreciable bioavailable DOP pool and ongoing ablation-derived supplies — are sufficient to meet algal P demand over timescales of days, arguing that previous claims of P limitation based on detection-limit artifacts likely overstate limitation.
meta.observable: Minimum dissolved inorganic phosphorus (DIP) concentration (nM) required to supply one day's P demand for observed glacier ice algal cell concentrations (cells/mL)

meta.conclusion: Under the implemented, literature-motivated parameterization, hydroclimate (aridity index AI) controls the sign of GPP sensitivity to cloud cover: below AI≈0.155 clouds tend to reduce GPP, and above that threshold clouds can increase GPP (Stage F: hedged due to parameter uncertainty).
meta.observable: dGPP/dCF at baseline cloud fraction CF=0.4 (units: gC m-2 day-1 per unit cloud fraction)

meta.conclusion: In this sampled set, 75% (6/8) of bacterial Teneurin-like proteins show RHS-like repeats or secretion/anchoring features consistent with Rhs/polymorphic toxin architectures, supporting the hypothesis that bacterial TLPs function as accessory/polymorphic toxins (provisional and sample-limited).
meta.observable: fraction_of_sampled_TLPs_with_RHS_or_secretion_features

meta.conclusion: Empirical relations (Raymer, Han) can deviate substantially (≈17% for clean sandstones; ≈26% for limestones) from a physics-based HS+Gassmann forward model across typical porosity ranges — suggesting caution when applying these empirical fits unvalidated in tectonically deformed mixed lithologies.
meta.observable: Mean absolute percent deviation of empirical-model Vp (Raymer or Han) relative to physics-based HS+Gassmann Vp across the tested porosity range

meta.conclusion: On this metadata-only proxy task (predicting 'cast'), the logistic-regression model trained on the dominant Siemens data did not show AUC decline on the small external set; external AUC ~0.6446 vs internal holdout AUC ~0.6083 (no degradation observed).
meta.observable: AUC difference (external AUC minus internal holdout AUC); ECE difference (external minus internal).
