The combined picture is that bulk P is not the seasonal bottleneck on average, but P (and to a lesser extent N) likely becomes rate-limiting in the upper tail of field growth rates and in localised patches of high cell density - consistent with the paper's own hedge that 'there are likely to be occasions when nutrient limitation occurs either locally or for periods of days'.
meta.observable: Implied P-uptake-constrained specific growth rate mu_max (d^-1) computed at the measured ambient [SRP] in unweathered ice and the weathering crust, with the ratio mu_max / mu_field as the limitation metric.

meta.conclusion: The hypothesis (a simple sign reversal: positive β in dry ecosystems, negative β in wet ecosystems) is REFUTED as originally stated. Across 24,760 valid land cells in 2001–2016, the bivariate GPP–cloud sensitivity β is negative on average (mean = −0.021 gC m⁻² month⁻¹ per %-cloud; median = −0.009) and the global correlation with aridity is extremely weak (Pearson r = 0.044, Spearman ρ = 0.021, both significant only because n is large). However, the relationship is non-monotonic: when cells are binned by aridity index, the sign of β flips from negative in the dryland range to POSITIVE in the humid range (peak β ≈ +0.09 at AI ≈ 1.7–2.0) before returning to slightly negative for very humid cells (AI > 2.5). The trough in β is in the dry sub-humid class (AI ≈ 0.5–0.65; β = −0.053), where clouds hurt GPP the most, not in the driest class as originally hypothesized. When the regression is re-specified to control for downward shortwave radiation (partial | DSWRF), the negative slope deepens everywhere (mean β = −0.041) and the relationship with aridity becomes weakly NEGATIVE (Spearman ρ = −0.086), indicating that the apparent positive β in humid regions is largely the direct-radiation shading effect of clouds rather than a diffuse-fertilization or VPD benefit. The defensible synthesis: at the monthly interannual scale, hydroclimate does NOT produce a sign-reversal in the simple GPP–cloud sensitivity. Instead, (i) in arid and semi-arid ecosystems, cloud cover uniformly depresses GPP, suggesting either that light remains a co-limiting factor or that the diffuse-radiation benefit does not reach the P-model's LUE formulation; (ii) in the most energy-limited humid ecosystems, the bivariate GPP–cloud sensitivity is mildly positive, consistent with diffuse-fertilization; and (iii) controlling for shortwave radiation wipes out the positive β, indicating the apparent positive sensitivity is a radiation-shading effect, not an LUE benefit.
meta.observable: GPP sensitivity to cloud cover β = ∂GPP_anom/∂TCDC_anom, computed as the per-cell OLS regression slope of monthly GPP anomalies (gC/m²/month) on monthly total cloud cover anomalies (%) over 2001–2016. Units: gC m⁻² month⁻¹ per %-cloud. Computed for 24,760 valid land cells at 0.5° resolution. The bin-mean β as a function of aridity is the key derived observable.

meta.conclusion: Bacterial Teneurin-like proteins are accessory toxins of polymorphic toxin systems, not passive sequence homologs of metazoan Teneurins. The YD-shell (PF25023) is the universal Rhs/TCAP toxin shell, present in 63/200 bacterial TLPs and structurally conserved between known bacterial Rhs toxins (RhsA-D, WapA, Burkholderia CDI toxin, Dickeya RhsA-C) and metazoan Teneurins. Critically, 24 bacterial TLPs (12%) have the exact TCAP toxin architecture (YD-shell + pretoxin HINT autoprotease), and 3 carry the actual Tox-GHH nuclease (PF15636) that is INACTIVELY present at the C-terminus of metazoan Teneurins. 173/200 (86.5%) have signal peptides consistent with secretion via T6SS/T7SS. Pfam explicitly notes that 'metazoan Teneurin proteins possess an inactive [copy] of Tox-GHH at their C-terminus' — meaning the metazoan Teneurin is a domesticated, catalytically-dead descendant of the bacterial TLP toxin. This strongly supports the open question's resolution: the bacterial TLP is a true Rhs/TCAP accessory toxin, and metazoan Teneurins evolved from it via HGT, losing the catalytic nuclease activity but retaining the YD-shell scaffold that was repurposed for cell-cell adhesion in the nervous system.
meta.observable: Domain architecture co-occurrence: the number of bacterial TLPs carrying (a) the Teneurin YD-shell (PF25023), (b) the Teneurin NHL propeller (PF25021), (c) the pretoxin-HINT (PF07591) autoproteolytic release domain, (d) the Tox-GHH nuclease (PF15636), (e) the RHS repeat (PF05593), and (f) the Salmonella SpvB virulence toxin domain (PF03534). Cross-validated against the 27 SwissProt reviewed YD-shell proteins to identify which are bacterial Rhs toxins vs metazoan Teneurins.

meta.conclusion: The standard empirical velocity-porosity models (Wyllie, Raymer, Han, Tosaya-Nur) do NOT predict sonic-log P-wave velocity with sufficient accuracy (<=10% bias) for either the Eocene carbonate or the Cambrian sandstone in the Missakeswal area: mean absolute bias across all four models and both units is 14.7% (Walton frame) / 16.3% (cemented frame), and every model exceeds 10% bias in at least one unit. Consequently, these models should not be used as the sole basis for reservoir-quality and hydrocarbon-saturation assessment in this structurally complex, mixed carbonate-siliciclastic setting; lithology-specific calibrated models (e.g. Xu-Payne carbonate rock physics templates) are required.
meta.observable: Percentage bias (100 * mean(observed - predicted)/observed) of empirical-model-predicted Vp versus Gassmann-substituted 'observed' Vp, reported per unit and per model. RMSE in km/s and R^2 also reported.

meta.conclusion: Calibration and overconfidence degrade under realistic distribution shift in musculoskeletal fracture AI much more than discrimination does, supporting the hypothesis that AUC is a misleading headline metric. In the view-shift experiment, AUC is unchanged (+0.0%) while ECE degrades by 54.5%; in the anatomy-shift experiment, AUC drops 22% while ECE drops 247% (~11× the relative magnitude). The clinically-actionable number — does a model that says '0.6 fracture probability' mean it 60% of the time? — collapses on out-of-distribution data even when discrimination is preserved. This helps explain the gap between orthopedic AI benchmark performance and clinical deployment: published papers report AUC near 0.85, but they almost never report calibration or subgroup recall, and our results suggest the calibration gap is the larger failure mode.
meta.observable: Pair-wise comparison of (AUC, ECE, Brier, per-subgroup recall) across: (a) internal i.i.d. test set, (b) external view-shifted test set, (c) external anatomy-shifted test set. The key derived observable is the ratio (relative change in calibration metric) / (relative change in AUC) when going from in-dist to out-of-dist; if >1, calibration degrades faster than discrimination.

meta.conclusion: On a planted AD ground truth, the branch-resolved PAS at lambda=0.5 correctly identifies the (CSF1, CSF1R, PI3K-AKT) triple as the top-1 branch at every lambda in [0, 1] (z = 9.03, p < 0.001), achieves top-5 accuracy of 1.00 vs 0.40 for the L-R-only baseline and 0.60 for the pathway-aggregate baseline, and is stable under 0.05-sigma noise (APRT = 1.0). Hypothesis supported. The shuffled-label negative control still returns 1.0 accuracy, however, which signals that the iS2C2 design is biased toward whichever pathway has the most downstream edges in the L-R + KEGG/IPA graph - a real-world risk that the iS2C2 paper does not address. The branch-resolved approach is more accurate than L-R-only or pathway-aggregate baselines in this setting, but the LLM half of the iS2C2 pipeline is not tested here (no API in the sandbox) and remains an open claim.
meta.observable: Top-5 accuracy (fraction of S2C2 top-5 (L, R, pathway) triples in the planted ground truth set) and permutation z-score of the top branch, measured at lambda=0.5 on the synthetic AD dataset with planted (CSF1, CSF1R, PI3K-AKT) ground truth.

meta.conclusion: Adult-derived methods partially transfer to paediatric cardiac surgery, with method choice being more important than in adult populations: regularised logistic regression beat every tree ensemble for LOS prediction (test AUROC 0.785 vs 0.762 for RF and 0.758 for tuned XGBoost; default XGBoost only 0.706). The 0.75 hypothesis threshold is met for LR and barely met for tree models, but the XGBoost default setting that wins on adult EHR data underperforms the trivial STAT-only baseline. For similarity retrieval, a triplet-loss embedding learned to (0.996 top-1) on the joint (diag + surgery) class but dropped to 0.469 on STAT category, whereas hand-crafted features scored 0.605 on STAT category, revealing that representations optimised for one clinical concept do not transfer to others. The methods that 'work' in adult populations do transfer, but the winning method is not the one a default-pipeline adult researcher would pick.
meta.observable: Test-set AUROC for prolonged-LOS classification, and test-set top-1 retrieval accuracy for clinically-similar patients (joint diagnosis + surgery type, defined as the primary clinical class)

meta.conclusion: The hypothesis is PARTIALLY supported: T_s and T_a are NOT equivalent at the daily, within-city level. A leave-one-city-out transfer model that uses only satellite-observable features to predict UHI_a achieves R^2=0.75 and MAE=0.47 degC, which is better than the naive proxy (UHI_a = UHI_s, MAE=0.54 degC, R^2=0.66) but still leaves large errors -- and 6 of 27 cities have |UHI_s - UHI_a| > 0.5 degC annually (Sydney: 1.01 degC). However, the very high annual-mean correlation (r=0.99) shows that T_s and T_a track each other well at climate-scale averages, so the proxy assumption is defensible for impact studies that use long-term climate averages but UNRELIABLE for daily or sub-daily UHI quantification.
meta.observable: Cross-city transfer MAE and R^2 of UHI_a prediction from satellite-observable features, vs. naive proxy baseline (UHI_a_pred = UHI_s). Also: per-city annual bias = UHI_s - UHI_a.

meta.conclusion: The 1SF linear-in-nu term captures ~74-80% of the exact equal-mass shift for two independent gauge-invariant observables -- substantial and domain-bridging, but short of the >=90% strong-hypothesis threshold; the remaining ~20-26% (a ~1% absolute effect in binding energy) requires second-order self-force, so 1SF bridges the extreme-mass-ratio and comparable-mass domains at the ~1% level but not to LISA's target accuracy without 2SF.
meta.observable: Fraction of the exact equal-mass (nu=1/4) shift captured by the 1SF linear-in-nu term, for two independent gauge-invariant observables: the ISCO frequency shift delta(nu) and the circular-orbit binding energy Ehat(x).

meta.conclusion: Zinc-transporter expression in pan-cancer tumors IS under coordinated upstream transcription-factor control: a 34-TF panel explains within-tissue transporter variance significantly above a variance-matched random-gene null (R2=0.19 vs 0.135, z=2.75, p=0.004), and the model recovers experimentally-validated regulatory links de novo (MTF1->ZnT1, NFKB1->ZIP8), with CREB1, MTF1, SP1 and NF-kB/RELA as dominant hub regulators; the effect is real but modest, so TF control is a genuine contributor rather than the sole driver of transporter dysregulation.
meta.observable: Cross-validated residual R^2 (variance of transporter expression explained by TF panel, tissue-adjusted) vs random-gene null

meta.conclusion: A downward Marangoni crown-shear force (~D^2) balancing buoyancy (~D^3) quantitatively reproduces the observed ~120 um critical escape diameter with an O(1) drag coefficient and measured surface velocities, confirming Marangoni shear trapping as the mechanism that keeps large bubbles entrained until they exceed the critical size.
meta.observable: Critical bubble escape diameter D_crit (um) at which upward buoyancy overcomes the downward Marangoni surface-shear force

meta.conclusion: All four parental factors are significant contributors with small-to-modest effect sizes, and parental digital use is reliably the largest (r~.28-.29, top in ~87% of resamples) while SES is negative (r~-.17 to -.20); cultural background plausibly moderates the parenting-behavior association (West > East, directionally consistent) but this moderator is underpowered (significant in only ~48% of resamples), and measurement sub-type does not reliably moderate any factor.
meta.observable: Pooled Pearson correlation r (with 95% CI, I2, tau2) per factor, and Q_between moderator statistics for culture and measurement sub-type

meta.conclusion: The itinerant Lindhard susceptibility of a realistic FeGe kagome model peaks at a finite incommensurate q_z (delta ~ 0.052 r.l.u., matching experiment) with the AFM point at a local minimum and a temperature-driven incommensurate-to-commensurate lock-in, supporting a Fermi-surface-nesting/SDW origin over a local-moment double-cone; the qualitative conclusion is robust across ~100 parameter sets, though the exact delta is parameter-tuned and the double-well depth is shallow (~1% of chi0), so this is strong corroboration rather than decisive quantitative proof.
meta.observable: peak wavevector of the static Lindhard susceptibility chi0(q_z) along c*, and its incommensurate displacement delta from the A-type-AFM point q_z=pi/c, in reciprocal lattice units of 2pi/c

meta.conclusion: A single global LSTM retains roughly 57-72% of its gauged high-flow F1 when evaluated on entirely held-out regions (bootstrap median ~0.60, right at the pre-registered 0.6 threshold; ~0.85 for tropical Brazil alone) and beats a persistence nowcast at every gauged lead while degrading smoothly, not collapsing; the evidence weakly-to-moderately supports the data-availability/generalization interpretation of the regional gap over intrinsic unpredictability, but the retention ratio sits at the falsification line (one bootstrap lead dipped to 0.57) and is regime-dependent (weak in snowmelt-dominated Chile), so we hedge rather than claim confirmation.
meta.observable: F1 score on return-period high-flow exceedance events, per lead time (0-6 days), separately for gauged (in-training-region, out-of-time) and ungauged-region (out-of-space+time) evaluation, and the ungauged/gauged F1 ratio.

meta.conclusion: Device-level stochastic volatile switching produces a tonotopic map in which N_ON is linear in log10(f) (R^2=0.95, slope 7.4 devices/decade) across 3 decades, outperforming a linear-in-f model, and stochasticity monotonically improves the map's linearity relative to a deterministic device, confirming the hypothesis.
meta.observable: N_ON(f): number of memristors switched ON within the 25 ms window as a function of input spike frequency f; the paper's stated observable is that N_ON increases linearly with the logarithm of input frequency.

meta.conclusion: The multifault network robustly reproduces the observed logarithmic (afterslip-driven) aftershock migration at ~0.7-1.2 km per decade, whereas a single plane instead produces a fluid-diffusion-like sqrt(t) front; this supports concurrently active fault strands whose afterslip, not fluid diffusion, drives aftershock expansion.
meta.observable: Aftershock-front migration law: R2 of front-radius fit to log10(t) vs sqrt(t), and cumulative area vs log(t) [afterslip] vs t [fluid diffusion]; plus emergent migration rate in km per decade of log10(time).

meta.conclusion: Ignoring competing non-CVD death causes 1-KM/Cox-style CVD risk estimates to overpredict true 10-year cumulative incidence by a margin that grows monotonically with age, negligible in the young (<0.1 pp) but reaching 6.7 pp at age 80-84 and 12.7 pp at 85+, whereas the Aalen-Johansen competing-risks estimator recovers the true risk unbiasedly, quantitatively confirming that competing-risk correction is essential for CVD risk prediction in the elderly.
meta.observable: Absolute overprediction of 10-year CVD cumulative incidence = (1 - Kaplan-Meier) minus true cause-specific cumulative incidence function (CIF), in percentage points, by age band

meta.conclusion: Supported with a boundary: cheap composition-only ML on ~40 sparse public UHTC melting points reaches CV MAE 204 K, R2 0.77, Spearman 0.86 and correctly rank-screens the record hypersonic candidates (top-8 8/8) whenever the query chemistry has ANY training analog -- so fragmented data is NOT the barrier the paper implies for screening; the barrier is specifically chemistry EXTRAPOLATION (no-analog families like actinide ThC inflate MAE to ~272 K), which cheap features cannot bridge and which is where new targeted data/simulation should be spent.
meta.observable: melting temperature T_m (K), cross-validated MAE / R2 / Spearman rank correlation

meta.conclusion: Glioblastoma malignant states are strongly, non-randomly and reproducibly spatially organized (same-state neighbor fraction ~0.60 vs 0.26 null, global z~77; replicated at z~23 in an independent section); all four states self-associate and mutually segregate, and hypoxia forms the dominant long-range organizing axis (Moran's I=0.85) tightly coupled to the MES-like state (r=0.87), which shows the strongest per-state coherence.
meta.observable: spatial coherence (fraction of same-state neighbor edges) and per-state join-count enrichment z-score vs a composition-preserving permutation null; hypoxia Moran's I

meta.conclusion: Functional annotations improve polygenic prediction substantially more at high SNP density than at low density (idealized: +6.4% vs +0.75%, interaction +5.65 pp, p=1.2e-5), a positive density x annotation interaction that vanishes under a shuffled-annotation control (p=0.93) and whose SIGN is robust at realistic enrichment (though magnitude/significance shrink), confirming the causal-variant/annotation-matching mechanism: dense panels unlock annotation value rather than merely adding to it.
meta.observable: Density x annotation interaction on prediction R^2: (relative annotation R^2 gain at high density) - (relative annotation R^2 gain at low density)

meta.conclusion: A deterministic OPSIN->RDKit tool converts IUPAC names to correct molecular structures with 96.1% exact-match accuracy versus 1.1% for a bare token-prediction LLM (Qwen2.5-7B) - a ~95-point gap that confirms LLMs cannot reliably perform this basic chemistry operation and that expert-tool augmentation is decisive.
meta.observable: IUPAC-name-to-SMILES exact-match structural accuracy (fraction of names converted to the canonically-correct molecular graph)

meta.conclusion: Single-reference DFT (BHandHLYP) puts the C13 triplet 0.46 eV (10.6 kcal/mol) below the singlet, but the broken-symmetry singlet carries strong diradical character (S^2=1.31) and, after Yamaguchi spin projection, the singlet drops to 0.30 kcal/mol (0.013 eV) BELOW the triplet -- i.e. the states are near-degenerate with the multireference-corrected singlet marginally lowest, consistent with CASSCF/CASPT2; the C13 singlet is a strongly kinked, heterogeneous ring (ring-angle spread 29 deg, angles 138-167 deg) versus the near-uniform aromatic C18 (spread 0.4 deg) and the near-uniform even dimer C26 (spread 0.8 deg), confirming that the localized kink defect is a signature of ODD-ring frustration that is relieved on dimerization to the even C26 ring.
meta.observable: adiabatic singlet-triplet energy gap DeltaE_ST(C13) [eV; E_singlet - E_triplet] at raw DFT and after spin projection, plus ring bond-length-alternation (BLA, Angstrom) and ring-angle spread (deg) as kink descriptors

meta.conclusion: Across the full algorithm panel, algorithm choice explains more accuracy variance than all tumor/data features combined on every SMC-Het observable (ratio 1.17x for co-clustering to ~40x for cluster count), reproducing the SMC-Het study's central finding; however this margin is task- and panel-dependent - among only competent methods, sequencing depth and purity dominate co-clustering and cellular-prevalence accuracy while algorithm choice keeps dominating the number-of-clusters task, and copy-number alteration is negligible throughout.
meta.observable: Fraction of total variance in reconstruction accuracy (SMC-Het SC1B/SC1C/SC2 scores) attributable to algorithm choice vs tumor/data features (eta-squared from ANOVA)

meta.conclusion: Multimodal fusion robustly improves multi-label dementia-etiology discrimination by +0.044 macro-AUROC (95% CI clear of the +0.03 bar; 0.041-0.045 across 5 seeds) over the best single modality, and matches-or-beats the best modality on every label; a same-capacity control (alignment destroyed) collapses to 0.587 and an adversarial variant where one modality is made sufficient collapses the fusion gain to +0.004, together showing the gain is genuine cross-modal complementarity rather than added parameters or a construction artifact. A label-noise sweep shows multimodal macro-AUROC rises to 0.806 at 5% and 0.918 at 0% noise, so the pre-registered 0.80 target is reachable and was missed at 0.74 only because of the 10% clinical-label-noise ceiling.
meta.observable: Macro-averaged AUROC across the 5 etiology labels (multi-label discrimination), and the paired delta of multimodal minus best-unimodal AUROC

meta.conclusion: mRNA explains only ~23% of protein-level variance in GBM (median cross-tumor rho=0.465 vs permutation null 0.07), and although measurement noise inflates this, the DECOUPLING IS BIOLOGICALLY STRUCTURED and survives independent noise-adjustment for large complexes (OXPHOS rho=0.12, ribosome rho=0.20) and strikingly affects key tumor suppressors (TP53 rho=0.18, PTEN rho=0.27) -- confirming a substantial, non-redundant proteomic regulatory layer invisible to transcriptomic/genomic profiling, which plausibly explains why genomic characterization alone has not delivered actionable GBM targets.
meta.observable: per-gene mRNA-protein Spearman correlation (rho) distribution across the proteome

meta.conclusion: Self-supervision provably learns transferable, label-efficient pathology features on held-out tissue (beating random-init and from-scratch), but at scales reproducible in this sandbox it does NOT beat ImageNet transfer and gets worse when the model is enlarged without proportional data; this indicates the published foundation-model rare-cancer advantage is real but critically SCALE-dependent (1.5M WSIs / 632M params), not an intrinsic property of self-supervision alone.
meta.observable: ROC-AUC of frozen-feature linear probe on held-out tumor-vs-normal, as a function of labels-per-class (label efficiency)

meta.conclusion: In the compact 177-bp fiber, H5's globular domain binds off-dyad: it is laterally translocated ~14 A from the symmetric on-dyad position and leans onto one DNA gyre (gyre-distance asymmetry rises from 3.4 A on-dyad to ~11 A off-dyad, a 3.2x increase), quantitatively reproducing the paper's reported ~15.2 A switch and confirming a context-dependent on-dyad-to-off-dyad transition upon fiber folding.
meta.observable: GD lateral translocation (on-dyad -> off-dyad, A) and GD gyre-distance asymmetry |d_topgyre - d_botgyre| (A)

meta.conclusion: The point-adjustment protocol inflates a no-skill random score to F1-PA 0.81-0.96 (SOTA-level) on SMD and shrinks the trained-vs-random gap to a negligible 0.084, whereas the threshold-free PR-AUC widens that gap ~4x to 0.32; therefore the PA-based SOTA F1 numbers pervading the surveyed deep-TSAD literature are largely an evaluation artifact, and any taxonomy/benchmark of these methods must be reported under PA-free metrics.
meta.observable: F1-PA (best-threshold point-adjusted F1) vs threshold-free PR-AUC, per detector, across machines

meta.conclusion: A parameter-free single-particle diffusion model reproduces the observed SC/PC rate gap (both ~190 mAh/g at 0.1C; SC->133, PC->192 at 5C) from diffusion-length geometry alone, so the reproducible baseline gap is ~10 mAh/g at 0.1C rising to ~60 mAh/g at 5C; a CEI claim is genuine only if it moves capacity beyond this geometric baseline.
meta.observable: Discharge specific capacity vs C-rate (mAh/g), and the SC-minus-PC capacity gap (mAh/g) at each rate = the transport-only baseline.

meta.conclusion: A smooth NN potential trained only on energies and forces reproduces the analytical (autodiff) TS Hessian to within 2.4% on the imaginary frequency, |cos|=1.00 reaction-mode overlap, 15 cm-1 vibrational MAE, and 0.6% full-matrix error -- energy/force training IS sufficient for reliable analytical Hessians, refuting the pessimistic conclusion.
meta.observable: imaginary (reaction-mode) frequency at the TS, full-spectrum vibrational-frequency MAE, and reaction-mode eigenvector overlap |cos theta|

meta.conclusion: On unseen single-gene perturbations, the learned model does NOT achieve a meaningful, consistent advantage over the mean-perturbation baseline: it wins DE-gene delta-Pearson by only +0.009 (negligible, ~1.7% relative) while being WORSE on DE-gene MSE and on the all-genes metric, so the central AIVC premise that learned representations capture generalizable perturbation mechanism is not supported by this test and the hypothesis is falsified in substance.
meta.observable: per-perturbation Pearson correlation of predicted vs true expression delta on top-20 differentially expressed genes (delta-Pearson on DE genes), for unseen perturbations, averaged over 8 held-out splits

meta.conclusion: Directly sequencing what grows on plates and matching it to the source community yields a proportion of cultivable taxa several-fold (paper ~3-6x; my model 9-19x) higher than the proportion of cultivable cells, and this gap is a depth-independent consequence of taxon- vs cell-weighting robust to how cultivability relates to abundance; the classical cell-based figure therefore severely underestimates taxon-level cultivability.
meta.observable: PCT (proportion of cultivable taxa) and its ratio to PCC (proportion of cultivable cells), computed directly from simulated sequencing of plate vs source communities

meta.conclusion: Both mechanisms hold, with one refinement: fused-ring count causally gates synthetic accessibility in a THRESHOLD (not linear) way -- a large penalty (0.43-0.73 SAscore/ring, Cohen d=1.58) appears only above ~2-3 fused rings, and TamGen's FDA-like fused count (recomputed 1.774, matching claimed 1.78) places it on the favorable SA plateau (0.79) that quantitatively predicts its reported SAS (0.771), while polycyclic 3D-generator output falls in the penalized regime (predicted 0.62 vs TargetDiff's 0.585); separately, VAE seeding from good compounds raises the joint multi-property score by ~76% over de novo sampling and increases diversity, with a random-seed control confirming the gain comes specifically from good seeds.
meta.observable: FDA-drug mean fused-ring count; Spearman rho(fused, SAS_norm); size-controlled per-ring SA penalty (hinge slope); Cohen d SA penalty (low vs high fused); refinement improvement in joint QED*SAS score (seeded vs de novo)

meta.conclusion: Infusing a molecular graph with GFN2-xTB stereoelectronic descriptors reduced GNN test error on two electronic QM9 targets (HOMO-LUMO gap by ~10.6%/20 meV, paired p=0.016, 5/6 seeds; dipole by ~6.0%, 4/4 seeds, p=0.082); two matched-capacity controls localize the cause -- a scrambled-feature control is decisively worse (p<0.01, both targets, ruling out capacity) and a geometry-only control is the worst condition with stereo beating it 4/4 seeds (ruling out generic 3D-geometry leakage) -- so the gain is attributable to genuine electronic information, supporting the SIMG premise, with the honest caveat that the effect is modest (6-11%) and only the 12k gap reaches conventional significance.
meta.observable: Test-set RMSE on QM9 HOMO-LUMO gap (Hartree), and the paired plain-minus-stereo RMSE difference across seeds.

meta.conclusion: The local two-elongation product is the EXACT loss gradient (cosine sim = 1.0, rel. error ~1e-8 for both MSE and cross-entropy), so a mechanical spring-lattice can be trained purely in situ from local information: it learns a vector-valued regression (test R^2=0.96), classifies Iris (76% test, capped by the single-layer linear regime below the 97% linear ceiling), is fully retrainable to a new task, and recovers accuracy (67%->78%) after a load-bearing bond is severed.
meta.observable: Primary: cosine similarity / relative L2 error between the local in-situ gradient (e_i*e_adj_i) and the brute-force finite-difference gradient. Secondary: test R^2 (regression) and classification accuracy through learning, retraining, damage, and recovery.

meta.conclusion: A completely damaged fNIRS channel can be reconstructed from surviving channels at r~0.85 (FC preserved at r~0.92), so such channels need NOT be discarded; however my central hypothesis is REFUTED: a generative CNN+GRU does not beat classical linear spatial imputation (it loses by delta r~0.25 within-subject), because the recoverable cross-channel structure is dominated by instantaneous linear spatial mixing that ridge captures optimally.
meta.observable: Mean Pearson correlation r between the reconstructed and ground-truth held-out channel time course (single-channel reconstruction fidelity), plus functional-connectivity matrix preservation r (edge-wise correlation of true vs reconstructed FC).

meta.conclusion: The result is regime-dependent: when phrasings fall within the RegEx author's anticipated vocabulary, RegEx matches or beats the LLM on recall/strict-F1 (my recall hypothesis is REFUTED there), but the LLM is consistently more accurate on the granular severity label (90% vs 81%); when phrasings drift out of that vocabulary (the realistic clinical case the paper targets), RegEx recall collapses to 0% while the LLM still recovers ~28% recall and wins 11/11 categories, confirming the paper's 'superior recall for diverse expressions' claim as a statement about generalization to unanticipated language rather than a universal edge.
meta.observable: Recall and strict F1 (detection AND correct DSM-5 severity) of SUD severity extraction, per substance category and micro-averaged, plus severity accuracy conditional on detection; LLM vs RegEx.

meta.conclusion: The sub-Chandrasekhar model variance CANNOT account for the observed super-solar [Mn/Fe] range: even at 3 Zsun the maximum sub-Ch [Mn/Fe] is -3.0 dex, ~3 dex below solar and ~3.4 dex below the Chandrasekhar value, because low central density forces alpha-rich freeze-out that suppresses 55Mn; the metallicity slope (~0.4 dex per factor-3 in Z) is orders of magnitude too shallow to close the gap.
meta.observable: [Mn/Fe] = log10(N_Mn/N_Fe) - log10(N_Mn/N_Fe)_sun, the iron-group production ratio, with Mn = 55Mn+55Co(+55Fe) and Fe = 54Fe+56Fe(+56Ni,56Co)+57Fe+58Fe by number

meta.conclusion: The minimum detectable subhalo mass is controlled overwhelmingly by stream DISTANCE (M_min ~ r0^2.9 for Gaia, a factor ~420 across 5-40 kpc) and secondarily by stellar density (~lambda^-0.85), while stream width and length are only weak drivers; a fast multivariate power-law estimator reproduces M_min with R^2=0.92-0.95, refuting the width-dominated hypothesis but confirming that a fast estimator exists and that nearby dense streams (e.g. GD-1: ~1e6 Msun for Gaia, ~2e5 for LSST) are the most sensitive probes.
meta.observable: M_min, the minimum detectable dark matter subhalo mass (Msun) at ~95% confidence level, and its power-law scaling exponents d(log M_min)/d(log X) for X in {width, length, distance, density}

meta.conclusion: The naive vacancy-formation-energy hierarchy is refuted (it is reference-dependent), but the reference-INDEPENDENT removal energy (Al 5.85 << C 10.95 < Ti 14.07 eV) and the realistic HF-etch thermodynamics (Al favorable -1.19 eV, C ~0, Ti +2.97 eV) both confirm a large, robust bond/energy hierarchy that makes Al selectively extractable while leaving Ti-C intact -- this is the atomistic mechanism that connects the HF-etch recipe to intact-flake quality.
meta.observable: Reference-free atom-removal energy E_remove (eV) for Al/C/Ti sites, and HF-etch reaction energy dE_etch (eV per removed atom) for Al->AlF3, Ti->TiF4, C->CH4.

meta.conclusion: cell2fate's linearized exponential-module transcription rate is genuinely closed-form (matches a stiff numerical solver to 3e-10) and ~120x faster per cell, while a handful of modules (M<=4) recovers the actually-measured spliced-count observable to within ~2-5% even for adversarial nonlinear/oscillatory transcription profiles that the modules fit poorly directly -- because splicing/degradation low-pass-filters transcription-rate error; so the flexibility-vs-tractability tension is largely resolved on the observable that matters.
meta.observable: spliced-count relative L2 error (s_cg, the measured scRNA-seq observable) and alpha(t) approximation relative L2 error as functions of module count M; plus closed-form-vs-numerical relative error and per-cell speedup

meta.conclusion: On multiclass (4-level) lameness detection with the CowScreeningDB sensor schema, a human-in-the-loop voting ensemble (deep model + interpretable gait features + veterinarian vote) is markedly more reliable than the black-box CNN alone (macro-F1 0.883 vs 0.767, worst-class recall 0.530 vs 0.362, F1 variance ~3x lower); however the improvement is driven mainly by the human-interpretable features and voting rather than the deep network, which alone is the weakest and most unstable component.
meta.observable: Macro-averaged F1 and worst-class recall for 4-level lameness classification, per system (DL alone, interpretable-features alone, DL+IF voting, full human-in-the-loop voting), averaged over cow-grouped CV folds.

meta.conclusion: Hypothesis REFUTED: the Holt-Winters decomposition front-end does not beat non-decomposing baselines on genuine next-day BTC forecasting (return RMSE and directional accuracy are statistically identical across LSTM/Transformer/Helformer and none beats a naive zero/persistence baseline); the paper's near-perfect R2~1.0 is reproduced by a no-parameter persistence forecast under whole-series price scaling, indicating it is a metric artifact of the price-level target rather than evidence of superior decomposition.
meta.observable: Next-day log-return RMSE and directional accuracy (sign hit-rate) on held-out test set; plus price-level RMSE/MAPE/R2 for comparison with the paper.

meta.conclusion: Lung-specific metastatic fate is governed by the STRENGTH of reciprocal tumor<->niche feedback rather than by initial seeding alone: above a critical coupling (beta_c~0.76) the coupled system is bistable and hysteretic (loop area 0.31), quantitatively formalizing why dormancy/reawakening is history-dependent and irreversible-appearing, whereas a one-directional seed-and-soil model produces no hysteresis (loop area 0).
meta.observable: Hysteresis loop area of steady-state tumor burden T* under forward/reverse sweep of niche priming; and the critical reciprocal coupling strength beta_c at the saddle-node bifurcation onset of bistability.

meta.conclusion: A label-free energy-residual PINN reproduces the entire von Mises shallow-truss equilibrium path including the unstable branch (1.64% L2) and auto-locates both limit points to <0.6% of rise in position, supporting the hypothesis; limit-point LOAD accuracy (~2.2-2.4%) marginally exceeds the 2% target and is the main caveat.
meta.observable: full load-displacement equilibrium path P(w) plus limit-point (snap-through) loads and their apex-descent positions

meta.conclusion: A self-driving lab's campaign time-to-target is governed by a single dominant physical bottleneck stage (react-stage elasticity 0.55 vs <=0.024 for all others, a 22.7x gap), and because campaign time is near-linear in experiment count, the algorithmic sample-efficiency lever dominates hardware-latency speedup (2x per doubling) once its acceleration factor exceeds AF~2 -- which the literature-typical AF~6 comfortably does, so in practice sample-efficiency is the larger lever; hardware investment wins only for near-random optimizers (AF<~2) or when a large fixed N-independent setup/calibration overhead is present; a unified SDL framework should therefore diagnose the bottleneck via stage elasticities and then prioritize sample-efficiency unless AF is low or fixed overhead binds.
meta.observable: campaign time-to-target T (wall-clock minutes to reach 95% of global-max property), and stage elasticity e_s = dlogT/dlog(latency_s); plus optimizer-upgrade gain vs hardware-speedup gain

meta.conclusion: Genus-level PD microbiome signatures are highly reproducible in direction across independent cohorts (r=0.83, all 10 literature genera concordant), but ML classifiers show only a modest generalization gap (~0.066 AUROC on average, direction-dependent and not statistically distinguishable from zero for logistic regression), remaining well above chance (p<0.001) rather than collapsing on transfer.
meta.observable: AUROC for PD-vs-control classification (within-study CV, cross-study transfer) and the within-minus-transfer generalization gap; plus cross-cohort directional concordance of per-genus differential abundance.

meta.conclusion: Over carbon-dense vegetated terrain a single explosive eruption is very likely a net carbon sink (median buried C ~12x the magmatic CO2 released, P(R>1)~0.99), independent of eruption magnitude; only over barren/sparsely-vegetated terrain does it revert to roughly carbon-neutral or a weak source, so the classic 'net source' view holds only where there is little landscape carbon to bury.
meta.observable: R = C_buried / C_emitted (sink-to-source carbon ratio per eruption, dimensionless)

meta.conclusion: The core DeepSPT premise holds directionally but conditionally: a deep model reading only raw trajectories beats a NAIVE summary-statistic baseline (D+alpha) by a large margin (+0.16 macro-F1, 0.62 vs 0.46), confirming DL can automatically extract functional diffusion structure that naive statistics miss; however it does NOT beat a well-engineered physics-informed feature set (-0.02 to -0.04 across all lengths) and neither method clears 0.85 in this deliberately-overlapping regime, so the hypothesis as stated is FALSIFIED on the '>=0.85 and beats classical by a wide margin' criterion while its underlying spirit (DL > naive analysis) is supported.
meta.observable: macro-averaged F1 score for 4-class diffusive-behavior classification (per trajectory)

meta.conclusion: An automated entailment+severity framework reproduces the hallucination/omission phenomenon and shows a self-verification prompt cuts hallucinations ~4x (major hallucinations 3.35->0.75) and lowers severity-weighted errors ~17% (49.45->41.15, p<0.001 paired); the per-claim hallucination rate also falls 0.43->0.20, so the gain is genuine faithfulness improvement, not merely shorter notes, at the cost of a small omission increase (21.4->23.8).
meta.observable: severity-weighted errors per note (and hallucinations/note, omissions/note, major hallucinations/note)

meta.conclusion: Model-agnosticism and multi-level integration coexist without trade-off: a single instance-label adapter benchmarked three structurally different networks on identical data (F1 spanning 0.656-0.989), and the downstream cascade was invariant to which accurate model was plugged in (organoid volume spread 0.0%, cell-territory ARI 0.982 between the two good models), while correctly degrading only when a genuinely weaker model was used (ARI 0.703) - so integration does not require locking the model.
meta.observable: Downstream-level invariance to plugged-in model: whole-organoid volume relative spread (%) across models, and L2 cell-territory Adjusted Rand Index between accurate models; alongside per-model nuclei F1@0.5.

meta.conclusion: A fundamental trade-off exists: dim(g) <= 4^n/F_eff - F_eff, and it is TIGHT — the SLPA saturates the upper bound with equality (gap = 0) in all 20 tested (n,s) cases, confirming F_eff=2^s and dim(g)=4^n/2^s - 2^s and thus a genuine measurement-efficiency-vs-expressivity Pareto frontier.
meta.observable: X_exp = dim(g) (dynamical Lie algebra dimension) and F_eff (mean number of simultaneously measurable gradient components = L/min(M_L))

meta.conclusion: Embedding the known measurement physics into the learned reconstructor gives a consistent PSNR advantage over an equal-capacity data-driven CNN (mean +2.4 dB at N<=5, peak +3.24 dB at N=5), and the advantage is largest under extreme data scarcity, supporting the claim that physical priors substitute for missing labeled data in medical image reconstruction.
meta.observable: Held-out test-set reconstruction PSNR (dB), and the PSNR gap (physics-informed minus data-driven) as a function of number of labeled training images.

meta.conclusion: exoPD-L1 is a competitive antibody sink whose neutralization cost scales LINEARLY (exponent ~1.0), not super-linearly, with secretion, so my quantitative super-linear claim is refuted; however the therapeutic-lever claim holds strongly: because the linear antibody demand is unbounded, at any finite clinical dose a high-exoPD-L1 tumor stays under-treated, and adding exosome-secretion inhibition yields a large non-redundant reactivation gain (+0.07 to +0.73 free-PD-1 fraction) unattainable by antibody escalation alone within realistic doses.
meta.observable: EC-dose scaling exponent d(log antibody_dose)/d(log exoPD-L1_secretion) to reach a fixed T-cell reactivation (free-PD-1 fraction), plus combo gain = free-PD-1(antibody+secretion-inhibitor) - free-PD-1(antibody alone) at finite dose

meta.conclusion: Lattice distortion broadens the vacancy migration-barrier distribution into a wide spread (std ~0.56 eV) with a genuine low-energy tail; this lowers the naive pool-averaged barrier to ~0.11 eV, but a connectivity-aware KMC shows low-barrier sites do not fully percolate, so the true network activation energy is much higher (1.2-3.0 eV, near the experimental range) - distortion controls the barrier landscape and provides accessible fast sites, offering a plausible mechanistic route to non-sluggish diffusion, though this atomistic toy model does not by itself prove net enhancement relative to pure elements.
meta.observable: Vacancy migration-barrier distribution (mean, std, low-tail) per element/alloy, its pool-averaged effective diffusion activation energy E_act_eff (eV), and the connectivity-aware KMC network activation energy (eV); plus RMS lattice distortion (Angstrom) per alloy.

meta.conclusion: DNMT1 binds unmethylated CpG DNA stably and at least as strongly as hemimethylated DNA in solution-representative MD (dG_bind -247 vs -205 kcal/mol; 228 vs 200 heavy-atom contacts; 23 vs 20 backbone salt bridges), with binding dominated by distributed electrostatic contacts to the DNA phosphate backbone -- reconciling the high-affinity solution measurements with the crystallographic 'weak-binding' snapshot, which reflects an autoinhibited/occluded state rather than an intrinsically weak UMDNA interface.
meta.observable: MM-GBSA binding free energy dG_bind (kcal/mol) for DNMT1-UMDNA and DNMT1-hemiDNA, and the relative ΔΔG_bind = dG(UMDNA) - dG(hemiDNA); plus electrostatic vs vdW component decomposition.

meta.conclusion: Adding raw DFT-tight-binding electronic descriptors (esp. polarizability, HOMO/LUMO, partial charges) to a 2D+host receptor-analyte recommender significantly improved within-host binding-affinity ranking on the SAMPL experimental benchmark (0.395 -> 0.533 mean within-host Spearman, +0.138, paired-bootstrap P=0.99, robust across seeds and helping 4/5 receptors), supporting the hypothesis that quantum information aids receptor-selectivity prediction; however, naive hand-engineered host-guest interaction cross-terms DEGRADED performance, so the benefit comes from raw first-principles descriptors, not from hand-crafted physics glue.
meta.observable: Mean within-host Spearman rank correlation between predicted and experimental binding free energy Delta_G (selectivity ranking accuracy), with top-1 tightest-binder hit-rate

meta.conclusion: Coarse, human-readable morphology (grade + histology type) adds essentially NOTHING (delta C-index +0.0015 Cox / +0.0002 GBSA, not consistently positive) beyond age+sex+stage in a unified pancancer model, even in early stage; therefore PROGPATH's reported ~+0.04 fusion gain must come almost entirely from a 'deep-learning premium' — sub-visual morphological signal a foundation-model+MIL pipeline extracts that standard pathology reads do not. This confirms the paper's core tension is real: routine clinical variables plus ordinary morphology already saturate at ~0.76, and any pancancer histopathology benefit is small, fragile, and cohort-dependent (PROGPATH itself gains only +0.012 on CPTAC and underperforms on CPTAC-PAAD/CCF-HNSC).
meta.observable: Harrell's concordance index (C-index) for overall survival, and its increment (delta C-index) from adding morphology features to a clinical-only baseline

meta.conclusion: Demographic heterogeneity reconciles the contradictory climate-migration findings: the small, unstable pooled weather effect is an aggregation artifact of opposite-signed subgroup responses (younger populations move less with heat, older low-education populations move more), and a demographically-interacted model recovers a ~7x out-of-sample predictive-skill gain that a pooled model cannot -- a gain that vanishes in a null control, confirming it is recovered signal rather than overfitting.
meta.observable: out-of-sample cross-validated R^2 of log migration rate on weather, for pooled vs demographically-heterogeneous models, and their ratio (heterogeneous/pooled predictive-skill gain factor)

meta.conclusion: FN-DMC and LNO-CCSD(T) agree to ~0.3-0.5 kcal/mol (bias -0.18), validating the reference; dispersion-corrected DFT (PBE+MBD, MAE 0.43) reproduces it while semiempirical GFN2-xTB (MAE 0.88, bias +0.62) and classical force fields (GAFF2 1.06/+0.85, CHARMM-CGenFF 1.77/+1.57, DFTB3+MBD 1.88/+1.88) all systematically UNDERbind by a statistically significant margin (p<1e-3).
meta.observable: Interaction energy E_int (kcal/mol) per dimer, and its mean absolute error (MAE) and mean signed error (bias) vs LNO-CCSD(T) across the 42 equilibrium dimers

meta.conclusion: The three terms are NOT empirically interchangeable: chance-corrected agreement is negligible-to-slight (kappa -0.01 to 0.16, all far below the 0.6 threshold), 36.6% of foods are classified differently by UPF vs hyper-palatable, and over half (51.4%) of non-ultra-processed foods are still hyper-palatable; the disagreement is chemically structured (McNemar p~1e-247), not noise, so the field's synonymous usage conflates a processing axis with a nutrient-reward axis and is unjustified.
meta.observable: Pairwise Cohen's kappa (and Jaccard) between the three binary food classifications, plus the fraction and nutrient structure of discordant foods

meta.conclusion: On real CITE-seq data the bio-conservation and batch-correction rankings are essentially uncorrelated (Spearman rho = 0.21, n=7) AND a Pareto-front check finds NO universal winner - only Harmony (bio-optimal) and totalVI (batch-optimal) are non-dominated, so improving batch correction requires sacrificing biological conservation and vice versa - confirming the bio-vs-batch tradeoff and 'no single best method' finding of the target benchmark.
meta.observable: Spearman rank correlation between per-method bio-conservation score and batch-correction score (scib-style), across the integration-method panel

meta.conclusion: Roughly 40-45% of the apparent benchmark signal is leakage/redundancy, not learning: a ligand-only model reaches R=0.71 on the core set (close to structure-based deep models at ~0.8) and 1-NN memorization alone reaches R=0.67, but under a leak-free clustered split the same model's R collapses from 0.67 to 0.38 (Delta R=0.29), confirming that reported performance is substantially inflated by train-test similarity.
meta.observable: Pearson correlation coefficient R (and RMSE, in pK units) between predicted and experimental -log(Kd/Ki) on the held-out set

meta.conclusion: Cavity-enhanced AFC memory efficiency follows eta=exp(-7/F^2) at impedance match (reaching ~90-93% for F>=8-10), but the AFC slow-light group delay grows ~13 ns per unit finesse -- so >90% efficiency requires a group delay of 2.5-3.7x the echo period, quantitatively confirming the efficiency/bandwidth-multimode tension; dispersion changes the predicted echo by 4.5-8.8x, so it cannot be neglected.
meta.observable: AFC storage (memory) efficiency eta; AFC-induced slow-light group delay tau_g relative to the echo time t_echo=1/Delta=42 ns.

meta.conclusion: Bulk-phase reacto-diffusive hydrolysis alone reproduces the observed SO2 uptake coefficient (gamma~0.09, obs 0.03-0.13); the air-water interface contributes only ~0.8% (<7% across all plausible parameters), so bulk chemistry dominates and no fast interfacial reaction is required.
meta.observable: reactive uptake coefficient gamma and the fractional interfacial contribution to total SO2 loss

meta.conclusion: Excited-state configuration -- whether the lowest nitroarene triplet is 3(pi,pi*) (ring-delocalized) or 3(n,pi*) (oxygen-lone-pair-localized), quantified by the hole density on the nitro oxygens -- rank-orders E->Z isomerization reactivity perfectly (Spearman rho=-1.00), whereas triplet energy does not (rho=-0.60) and loses its apparent signal under partial-correlation control (r drops -0.71 -> -0.27); the E_T-matching criterion cannot explain why the two highest-E_T catalysts (N33, N15) are the poorest, but the n,pi*/pi,pi* configuration ordering can.
meta.observable: T1 excited-state configuration (n,pi* vs pi,pi*, quantified by hole_O on the nitro oxygens) and DeltaE_TT = E_T(pi,pi*)-E_T(n,pi*), correlated against experimental %Z at the photostationary state.

meta.conclusion: K48-linked diubiquitin samples a significantly more compact ensemble with greater Ile44-patch burial than K11 (Rg Cliff's delta -0.65, patch-exposure delta -0.48, both p<1e-300, K48 median Rg 17.2 A matching experiment), supporting the hypothesis that linkage-encoded chain compactness / hydrophobic-patch accessibility is a physical signal by which the ubiquitin system can discriminate K48 from K11.
meta.observable: radius of gyration (Rg) of the diubiquitin CA trace, and Ile44-patch (L8/I44/V70) solvent exposure (number of patch atoms not occluded by the partner ubiquitin)

meta.conclusion: The linear proportionality Delta-k proportional to M0 is not an empirical fit but a DETERMINISTIC emergent consequence of cubic-law dilation plus A~V^(2/3) rupture scaling: a mechanistic per-event Monte-Carlo built from crack physics (no linearity assumed) recovers slope 1.000 across 13 decades of moment and matches the closed form dk = M0 dtau^2 tan^3(i)/(12 s G^3) exactly under the paper's moment-volume closure; the linearity is universal while the prefactor is closure-dependent.
meta.observable: Permeability change per unit seismic moment, dk/M0 (m^2 per N*m), and the log-log slope of cumulative Delta-k versus cumulative seismic moment M0.

meta.conclusion: In a realistic single-junction perovskite cell the optical J_sc loss is only ~3.2 mA/cm2 below the SQ limit (28.0), and front reflection accounts for ~87% of it (2.8 mA/cm2) while parasitic absorption in the electrode/transport layers is minor (~0.4) and perovskite bulk transmission is negligible (~0); thus the 'unresolved optical loss' is dominated by broadband Fresnel front reflection, not incomplete bulk absorption.
meta.observable: Supra-bandgap J_sc loss budget (mA/cm2): J_loss,reflection, J_loss,parasitic (per layer), J_loss,transmission, and useful perovskite-absorbed J_sc vs the Shockley-Queisser limiting current.

meta.conclusion: Whether a tissue 'has lymphatics' is a resolvable marker-specificity problem, not a genuine biological absence: single-marker LYVE-1 detection misclassifies 39% of macrophages as lymphatic (macro-F1 0.39, near the 0.33 chance floor), which is exactly why the bone/disc avascular dogma persisted; requiring co-expression collapses macrophage false positives to 0.26% (LEC precision 0.99) and multi-marker classification separates LEC/BEC/macrophages at macro-F1 0.87 — so the recent overturning of the dogma reflects a methodological upgrade from single-marker to co-expression detection rather than any new tissue.
meta.observable: macrophage false-positive fraction in the LYVE1-only 'lymphatic' gate, and macro-F1 (LEC vs BEC vs MAC) as a function of marker-panel size

meta.conclusion: Ablation of nanomolar-concentration ice supplies P in excess of bloom demand at both NW Greenland sites (median supply/demand 1.5-2.1x; P(sufficient) 79-91%), so phosphorus is not seasonally limiting once the melt flux is accounted for; nitrogen is close to balanced from inorganic N alone and requires the organic pool to be clearly in surplus.
meta.observable: Required ablation (cm of ice-water-equivalent melt) to supply bloom nutrient demand, and its ratio to actual seasonal ablation (supply/demand ratio); P(supply >= demand).

meta.conclusion: Background hydroclimate systematically controls the sign and strength of GPP sensitivity to cloud cover: sensitivity rises monotonically from strongly negative in humid energy-limited ecosystems (mean S=-0.24, 97% negative) toward positive in the most water-limited ecosystems (driest bin mean S=+0.03), with a highly significant cross-site decline of S with humidity (Spearman rho=-0.52, p~6e-11), confirming the hypothesized hydroclimatic control and sign flip.
meta.observable: S = dGPP*/dCF* (partial sensitivity of standardized monthly GPP anomaly to standardized cloud-fraction anomaly), and its cross-site relationship with humidity index HI.

meta.conclusion: Bacterial TLPs carry the diagnostic signature of polymorphic accessory toxins - a strongly conserved YD/RHS delivery shell (56% id, 1.75 bits) bolted to a hypervariable, poorly-alignable C-terminal payload (33% id, 2.79 bits, 0.13 occupancy) with a small cognate immunity gene directly downstream - so the ancestor of the neuronal Teneurin receptor was most likely a bacterial contact-dependent toxin-delivery protein.
meta.observable: Region-specific sequence conservation contrast between the YD/RHS shell and the C-terminal domain (mean percent identity to consensus, Shannon entropy, and alignment occupancy), i.e. the polymorphic-toxin variability signature.

meta.conclusion: Standard empirical velocity-porosity-density models transfer acceptably to the Cambrian Khewra sandstone (Vp MAPE 2.6-9.7%, correct negative Vp-porosity trend) but systematically underpredict the Eocene Sakesar/Chorgali carbonate Vp by ~1350-1770 m/s (MAPE 19-25%) and Castagna's mudrock line mis-predicts carbonate Vs by ~49%, so the models must be recalibrated (pore-type/Greenberg-Castagna-limestone) before use in this mixed carbonate-siliciclastic thrust belt.
meta.observable: Per-model P-wave velocity (and Vs, density) prediction error: MAPE (%), mean bias (m/s), R2, for each lithology.

meta.conclusion: Confirmed: under realistic acquisition shift the fracture model's calibration degrades far more than its discrimination (median R=32.7, always >1; up to R=125 in the mild-shift regime where AUC stays clinically usable at ~0.92), and clean-fit temperature scaling fails to repair shifted ECE (-4.6%) - so headline AUC masks a hidden, non-trivially-fixable calibration failure that is a genuine barrier to clinical translation.
meta.observable: Calibration-vs-discrimination degradation ratio R = (relative ECE increase) / (relative AUC drop) under distribution shift, plus fraction of shifted ECE removed by clean-fit temperature scaling.

meta.conclusion: Downstream target-gene response evidence recovers the truly-active ligand-receptor route (accuracy ~1.0) precisely in the converging/ambiguous regime where L-R-expression-only scoring degrades to chance (~0.50), and it fails gracefully to chance only when there is genuinely no downstream difference to detect; a real-data PBMC check confirms matched downstream modules couple to their sensor far more than equally-present decoy modules (delta r=0.38) — supporting iS2C2's core mechanistic premise that modeling downstream regulatory pathways adds route-discriminating information beyond ligand-receptor expression.
meta.observable: route-disambiguation accuracy (fraction of conditions the truly-active L-R route is ranked above the decoy) versus L-R expression ambiguity, and real-data pathway-activity delta-r between matched and mismatched downstream modules

meta.conclusion: Adult-style simplicity is suboptimal but not catastrophic for paediatric cardiology, and the two claimed benefits are decoupled: the LOS-accuracy gain (~0.7 day lower MedAE) comes almost entirely from LOCAL per-phenogroup modelling (not the mixed-type distance), while the mixed-type distance's contribution is confined to better outcome-relevant patient retrieval (+0.055 LOS-tercile purity), an advantage that grows as the outcome becomes more age-driven -- so a paediatric similarity pipeline helps, but retrieval quality and prediction accuracy must be credited to different components.
meta.observable: LOS median absolute error (MedAE, days) and k-NN retrieval purity (fraction of neighbours sharing LOS tercile / hidden phenogroup)

meta.conclusion: T_s and T_a co-vary strongly in TIME (r~0.9) but the surface UHI is NOT a transferable proxy for the air UHI: the daytime SUHI/CUHI ratio ranges from ~0 to ~12 (opposite signs in some cities), a naive T_s=T_a proxy misestimates the daytime air UHI by 1.3 degC RMSE (~85% of the signal), and even a cross-city ML transfer model leaves 0.9 degC error (R2=0.51 by day) and fails outright in some cities - confirming large, city-specific air/surface temperature discrepancies.
meta.observable: SUHI/CUHI ratio and leave-one-city-out transfer RMSE / R2 for predicting the air UHI (CUHI) from the surface UHI (SUHI)

meta.conclusion: Alpha-beta calibration fails to bridge the PN-ppBHPT gap by a factor of ~10^6: the fundamental issue is that PN uses total mass as its scale while ppBHPT uses primary mass, creating irreconcilable differences in velocity parameter and phase accumulation that cannot be absorbed by simple amplitude rescaling and constant phase shift. This confirms that the intermediate mass-ratio regime (q~2-10) remains a significant challenge for LISA waveform modeling, requiring either full numerical relativity or multi-parameter surrogate models that capture the full frequency-dependent structure of self-force corrections.
meta.observable: noise-weighted waveform mismatch optimized over coalescence time and phase

meta.conclusion: The Marangoni shear-stress retention model predicts a critical bubble diameter of 184 μm for RR1000 Ni superalloy at U=0.3 m/s and D=200 μm. The model captures the R² vs R³ scaling crossing that creates the observed sharp retention threshold at ~120 μm, with agreement within a factor of ~1.4 (error ~40%). The mechanism is the characteristic shear rate γ̇ = U/D acting on the bubble's projected area; smaller bubbles (R < R_crit) are retained while larger ones escape by buoyancy. Pool depth D = 306 μm would give exact agreement.
meta.observable: critical_bubble_diameter

meta.conclusion: Parental digital use shows the strongest association with preschooler prolonged digital use (r ≈ 0.23–0.24), independently corroborated across two meta-analyses; all four parental risk factors fall within the small-to-moderate range (r = 0.10–0.24), but sub-item measurement type does NOT moderate effect sizes (contradicted by independent evidence), and cultural background cannot be evaluated with retrieved data.
meta.observable: Difference in pooled correlation coefficients (Δz in Fisher's z space) between two independent meta-analytic estimates

meta.conclusion: The itinerant nesting mechanism produces an incommensurate wavevector q_nest = (0, 0, 0.35) with δ=0.15, which is qualitatively correct (incommensurate order emerges from Fermi surface topology) but quantitatively deviates from the experimental q_IC ≈ (0, 0, 0.42) with δ≈0.08, suggesting that while itinerant physics contributes, the full picture likely requires hybridization with local-moment effects or corrections to the simplified band model
meta.observable: Nesting wavevector q_nest where Lindhard susceptibility χ₀(q) peaks, and comparison to experimental incommensurate ordering vector q_IC and local-moment model predictions

meta.conclusion: A volatile memristor array with logarithmically graded relaxation times maps temporal input frequency to spatial voltage position with Pearson r = −1.0 (perfect monotonicity) and mean position error of 0.8% (deterministic) to 5.7% (stochastic) of array size, demonstrating that device-level stochastic switching naturally performs tonotopic encoding without any CMOS circuitry or explicit weight programming — a mapping mechanism directly analogous to the biological cochlea.
meta.observable: half-max position of steady-state activation pattern along device array (device index), mapped against log10(input frequency)

meta.conclusion: Gaussian mixture model analysis of 2749 Tohoku aftershocks reveals that all 8 along-strike bins show statistically significant multimodal depth distributions (k≥2, median k=4), with component separations of 2.5σ (median) and 98-100% bootstrap robustness, supporting the hypothesis that seismic slip is distributed across multiple concurrently active fault strands rather than a single detachment plane.
meta.observable: Number of GMM components (k) in depth distribution per along-strike bin

meta.conclusion: Adding emerging risk factors (COPD, cancer, pre-eclampsia) to CVD prediction models provides minimal calibration improvement (<1% reduction in error). However, applying Fine-Gray competing-risks adjustment transforms severe overprediction in 75+ populations (+16.4% → -18.2%) into mild underprediction, achieving a 5.3% population-wide calibration improvement. The competing-risk correction, not the emerging predictors, is the primary driver of improved accuracy in elderly patients.
meta.observable: 10-year CVD event probability (cumulative incidence) and age-stratified calibration ratio (observed/predicted)

meta.conclusion: High-entropy TMB2 compositions dramatically outperform monolithic ZrB2 (HSI improvement ~7-10%) but provide roughly PARITY with the already-effective ZrB2-20SiC baseline. The optimal strategy is a refractory-oxide-rich multi-cation (Zr-Hf-Ta) diboride with 20 vol% SiC, which achieves performance equivalent to HE-SiC with lower processing complexity. HE+SiC synergy exists mechanistically but is overwhelmed by the dominance of the borosilicate glass protection factor.
meta.observable: Hypersonic Survivability Index (HSI) — dimensionless margin ratio: HSI = (critical_recession / actual_recession) - 1. HSI > 0 means survival; HSI < 0 means failure.

meta.conclusion: Oxygen gradients alone do not generate the multi-layered spatial architecture observed in glioblastoma - the mechanistic simulation produced only weak, non-significant spatial correlation (ρ = 0.04, not significant) despite realistic oxygen diffusion and cell state transitions, suggesting that additional mechanisms beyond hypoxia-driven state transitions are required to produce the consistent layered organization reported in spatial transcriptomics studies
meta.observable: Spearman rank correlation coefficient (ρ) between cell state (ordered by hypoxia preference: OPC=1 < AC=2 < NPC=3 < MES=4) and distance to nearest necrotic region

meta.conclusion: Jointly modeling 7M common SNPs with functional annotations improves polygenic prediction by 27.4% relative to standard 1M HapMap3 approaches at realistic GWAS sample sizes (N=300K), with the improvement driven jointly by increased SNP density (15.8%) and annotation-informed priors (additional 10%), and the benefit increases in underrepresented populations.
meta.observable: Prediction R² (proportion of phenotypic variance explained by polygenic risk score in independent test sample)

meta.conclusion: Algorithm choice explains 54.4% of reconstruction accuracy variance, exceeding the 37.5% explained by tumor properties, but simple parametric methods (GMM) outperform Bayesian nonparametric approaches in 4/5 scenarios, suggesting algorithmic fit to the data-generating process matters more than algorithmic sophistication.
meta.observable: Pearson correlation between true and predicted cancer cell fractions (CCF), adjusted Rand index (ARI) for clonal assignment accuracy, variance decomposition (sum of squares) for algorithmic vs. tumor-intrinsic effects

meta.conclusion: Multi-label classification significantly outperforms single-label classification on mixed-dementia cases by +0.0413 AUROC (p<0.0001), supporting the hypothesis that modeling co-occurring pathologies improves differential diagnosis when trained on routinely available multimodal clinical data.
meta.observable: Micro-averaged AUROC on mixed-dementia subgroup and overall

meta.conclusion: The direction of the hypothesis is nominally supported (multi-tissue > single-tissue at 5-shot), but the magnitudes are pathological — multi-tissue collapsed and single-tissue is sub-chance — so no honest inference can be drawn about whether diversity actually helps for rare cancers. The result does not disconfirm the hypothesis; it reveals that my experimental benchmark is insufficient to adjudicate it. Real validation requires either (i) the full NCT-CRC-HE-100K dataset on real H&E patches, or (ii) careful calibration of the synthetic class prior so that frozen-backbone few-shot eval is actually discriminative, not a coin-flip against a fixed prior.
meta.observable: few_shot_top1_accuracy on held-out rare tissues (mean ± std across 10 random k-shot samplings)

meta.conclusion: On-dyad symmetric binding of linker histone H5 produces 97-fold better geometric regularity in chromatin fiber formation compared to off-dyad asymmetric binding, with RMS linker connectivity error of 0.002 nm vs 0.194 nm, demonstrating that symmetric binding is structurally necessary for stable 30-nm fiber architecture.
meta.observable: Linker DNA connectivity error (RMS deviation between actual linker length and required linker length to connect consecutive nucleosomes in helical fiber)

meta.conclusion: Architectural backbone matters 42x more than representation learning objective for time series anomaly detection performance (0.1791 vs 0.0042 ROC-AUC variance), rejecting the hypothesis that representation strategy dominates. However, confidence is LOW due to synthetic data limitations and narrow objective coverage (only reconstruction and contrastive tested).
meta.observable: variance in ROC-AUC across models grouped by architecture vs objective

meta.conclusion: Neural network potentials trained on energy and force data (without explicit Hessian supervision) produce analytical Hessians with correct eigenvalue signature at transition states, achieving 4-5/14 optimization success (80-100% of oracle performance) with sub-0.02 accuracy in saddle point location; contrary to Denzel et al.'s negative findings, this demonstrates feasibility when the potential is sufficiently smooth and trained with force supervision, though energy-only training also achieved equivalent success (5/14) on this simple 2D test system, suggesting the negative result may be specific to high-dimensional molecular systems.
meta.observable: Hessian eigenvalue signature (number of negative eigenvalues / imaginary frequencies) at saddle points; transition state optimization success rate (fraction of starting points converging within 0.1 distance units of true saddle); Frobenius norm relative error of analytical Hessian matrix

meta.conclusion: Mechanistic inductive bias is essential for out-of-distribution generalization in cellular dynamics prediction: an incomplete mechanistic ODE (RMSE=2.80) outperformed a perturbation-aware pure Neural ODE (RMSE=3.36) on unseen strong perturbations, supporting the hypothesis that hybrid approaches combining mechanistic structure with learned components are necessary for scalable virtual cell models. However, this conclusion is based on synthetic data and single-seed training; real-world validation remains essential.
meta.observable: out-of-distribution RMSE of predicted vs true state trajectory across all 12 variables and 50 time points across 10 unseen test conditions

meta.conclusion: The canonical ~1% 'great plate count anomaly' is a measurement artifact: at a uniform 1% per-cell cultivability, 83.1% of taxa in a log-normal community are analytically predicted to be cultivable (PCT/PCC ratio ≈ 83×). Even under heterogeneous cultivability with half of taxa truly uncultivable, PCT still reaches ~44% at ~0.3% PCC (ratio ≈ 153×). Sequencing-guided re-estimation of cultivability at the taxon level therefore reveals that environmental bacteria are far more cultivable than conventionally claimed — the 'uncultivable majority' is largely an illusion produced by conflating cell-level and taxon-level measurements of the same plate counts.
meta.observable: Ratio of PCT (proportion of cultivable taxa, defined as mean over taxa of P(at least one cell from taxon i is cultivable)) to PCC (proportion of cultivable cells, = E_abundance-weighted[p_i]), both expressed as percentages.

meta.conclusion: An iterative Pareto-based refinement mechanism raises the simultaneous-triple-threshold hit rate from 2.52% (Vina-only baseline) to 36.96% — a 14.66× improvement — supporting the TamGen paper's central claim that an integrated refinement mechanism materially improves the practical viability of target-aware generative drug design, though the improvement rests on an empirical binding model and a fragment-based SMILES representation rather than true covalent bond formation or structure-based docking.
meta.observable: success_rate_percent (fraction of selected molecules satisfying QED ≥ 0.6 AND SA ≤ 3.5 AND Vina ≤ −7.5 kcal/mol)

meta.conclusion: With information leakage corrected, only HOMO-LUMO gap prediction benefits from indirect stereoelectronic features (28.3% RMSE improvement, exceeding the 15% threshold), while dipole moment prediction is actively harmed (-26%) and molecular weight is unaffected (~0%). The hypothesis is PARTIALLY supported: stereoelectronic priors (NAO charges, Wiberg bond indices, orbital s/p/d fractions) genuinely encode orbital-interaction information relevant to molecular orbital energetics (HOMO-LUMO gap), but they do NOT encode the 3D orientation-dependent charge distribution information needed for dipole prediction. This selective benefit pattern strongly suggests the features are chemically meaningful (not generic capacity) — they help specifically for orbital-energetics properties.
meta.observable: RMSE reduction percentage (graph vs. graph+stereoelectronic) in predicting DFT-computed target properties

meta.conclusion: Mechanical neural networks CAN be trained in situ using equilibrium propagation with fully-local spring stiffness updates — achieving 100% accuracy on XOR across 5 random initializations, 77% on 4-bit parity, 37.5% on 4-class classification (vs. 25% random baseline), 100% accuracy when retrained from XOR to AND, and restoring XOR to 100% accuracy after 20% random spring removal — demonstrating vector-valued learning, retrainability, and damage recovery using only local information measured at each spring's endpoints, without global backpropagation of error gradients.
meta.observable: classification accuracy on benchmark tasks (XOR, 4-bit parity, 4-class vector classification) and accuracy-before/after/after-recovery for damage experiments

meta.conclusion: The 1D CNN achieves mean correlation of 0.639, outperforming the baseline by 0.005 (p=0.1571). The model shows promise but has not yet achieved the hypothesized improvement threshold.
meta.observable: Pearson correlation coefficient between reconstructed and ground-truth HbO time series

meta.conclusion: The hypothesis is REFUTED. While BioClinicalBERT achieved perfect classification (1.000 F1), so did all strong traditional NLP baselines (TF-IDF + SVM, TF-IDF + Naive Bayes), meaning the language model provides ZERO advantage over traditional methods. Error analysis reveals the dataset contains obvious shortcuts: severe notes are 2.5x longer (107 vs 43 words), 86% contain explicit severe keywords (homeless, unemployed, overdose), and DSM-5 criteria counts correlate strongly with severity. The synthetic dataset is too easy and fails to capture the true challenge of clinical language variability that the paper describes.
meta.observable: Macro-averaged F1 score for 3-class severity classification (mild/moderate/severe)

meta.conclusion: Metallicity-dependent neutron excess alone CAN explain most (85%) of the observed [Mn/Fe] scatter and MORE than all (265%) of the observed [Ni/Fe] scatter for physically realistic progenitor metallicities (Z = 0.5-2.0 Z_sol), contradicting the initial hypothesis; additional neutron sources like enhanced 25Mg or 13C are NOT required within current observational uncertainties.
meta.observable: [Mn/Fe] and [Ni/Fe] abundance ratios in dex, computed as log10 of ejecta number ratios relative to solar

meta.conclusion: A calibrated semi-empirical estimator predicts that GD-1 remains the most sensitive stream for subhalo detection (M_min = 6e6 Msun with Gaia, 8e5 Msun with LSST), with Helmi and Pal-5 as close runners-up; LSST will improve sensitivity by ~11x on average, enabling all 27 known Milky Way streams to probe subhalos at 10^7 Msun, but only GD-1 reaches 10^6 Msun — confirming that the growing stream catalog significantly expands dark matter substructure probes but falls short of the 10^5–10^6 Msun regime where CDM predicts abundant subhalos.
meta.observable: M_min (minimum detectable dark matter subhalo mass in solar masses Msun)

meta.conclusion: Computational kinetic modeling predicts that Ti vacancy defect density in MILD-synthesized Ti3C2Tx increases by a factor of 23.3 as etching temperature rises from 35°C to 80°C (from 0.13% to 3.06%), because the activation barrier for defect-forming Ti dissolution (1.22 eV) exceeds the overall Al-etching barrier (0.56 eV), progressively degrading dissolution selectivity with temperature; this provides a quantitative, falsifiable rationale for preferring low-temperature MILD synthesis (~35-44°C) for healthcare-grade MXene flakes.
meta.observable: Ti vacancy defect density (percentage of Ti lattice sites that are vacant) as a function of etching temperature

meta.conclusion: Piecewise-polynomial alpha(t) does NOT improve RNA velocity accuracy (it catastrophically overfits, MSE=29.4x stepwise-constant) and so is rejected; however piecewise-linear alpha(t) achieves 41% lower cell-fate-prediction error than stepwise-constant (MAE 0.249 vs 0.424), despite slightly worse in-sample fit, and does so at half the per-call evaluation cost (3.3 vs 6.4 ms) and half the fitting time (22 vs 40 s) — so the original hypothesis is PARTIALLY confirmed but the mechanism is regularization via interpolation smoothing (implicit bias-variance tradeoff), not the improved functional approximation we originally assumed.
meta.observable: Cell-fate-prediction MAE on the downstream extrapolation window (last 30% of timepoints), as the RNA velocity v(t)=beta*u(t)-gamma*s(t)

meta.conclusion: A heterogeneous deep learning ensemble (CNN+LSTM+Transformer) with biomechanically interpretable gait features achieves 75.6% accuracy on 4-class multiclass lameness detection—11.1 percentage points above a raw black-box CNN baseline (64.6%)—while a human-in-the-loop confidence thresholding mechanism successfully identifies low-confidence predictions (25% of cases flagged, showing 60% accuracy vs 81% for high-confidence predictions), and SHAP analysis confirms that biomechanical features (stance ratio, stride variability, peak asymmetry) drive 45% of model decisions, collectively demonstrating improved reliability, reduced black-box opacity, and actionable uncertainty quantification, though the modest absolute accuracy reflects the genuine difficulty of multiclass lameness assessment and suggests remaining limitations around class imbalance, label noise, and intra-class biological variability.
meta.observable: Multiclass classification accuracy and F1-macro for 4-level lameness detection, plus HITL flag rate and confident-vs-flagged accuracy differential

meta.conclusion: Helformer's explicit decomposition strategy provides modest improvement (6.94% MAPE reduction) over vanilla Transformer on short-term (7-day) forecasts, but underperforms LSTM across all horizons and fails to improve on longer-term forecasts, suggesting that sequential architectures may be better suited than decomposition-based attention for cryptocurrency price prediction
meta.observable: Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) across 7, 14, and 30-day forecast horizons

meta.conclusion: Lung metastasis is coevolutionary in character but NOT predominantly feedback-driven: the CTC survival/extravasation 'metastatic bottleneck' (intrinsic, 59%) and the exosome-niche-inflammation-reawakening feedback loop (41%) contribute comparably to lung-specific metastatic outcome, with extensive interaction (76% of explained variance is shared) — meaning positive feedback amplifies the intrinsic bottleneck rather than dominating it.
meta.observable: Log10 of active metastatic foci count at day 120 (log10(M_a + 1)), the standard 'metastatic burden' metric in this field

meta.conclusion: An energy-based PINN surrogate — parametrizing strain energy U(ξ) and recovering load by automatic differentiation P=dU/dξ — traces the complete nonlinear equilibrium path of the 30° von Mises shallow truss with mean absolute error 5.2×10⁻⁵ and locates the snap-through limit load to 0.0024% error, validating the hypothesis that a mesh-free physics-informed surrogate can replace arc-length FEM for full-path tracing and automatic critical-point identification without expert step tuning.
meta.observable: Equilibrium path P̄(ξ) and its critical (limit) points — the snap-through load P̄_snap where dP̄/dξ = 0 (sign change +→-) and associated normalized displacement ξ_snap. Also the full post-buckling trajectory including the snap-back minimum.

meta.conclusion: In a parametric model that treats the four SDL fragmentation dimensions symmetrically, data-format unification yields the largest single-cycle time saving (≈2.3 h off a 13 h fragmented baseline, 17%) and wins the ablation ranking in 4 of 6 counterfactual coefficient scenarios; however, the dominance is NOT absolute — it inverts when APIs are structured superlinearly or validation coefficients are elevated, so the field should treat format standardization as the empirically most likely (but not guaranteed) single highest-leverage intervention rather than an unconditional rule.
meta.observable: SDL single-cycle time (hours) and per-bottleneck ablation improvement (hours saved by unifying that dimension from fragmented baseline)

meta.conclusion: PENDING: To be completed after computational analysis
meta.observable: ROC-AUC (area under receiver operating characteristic curve) for PD vs healthy control classification

meta.conclusion: Monte Carlo analysis of two well-constrained explosive eruptions shows that tephra burial likely sequesters 1.5–11.5 times more soil organic carbon than the CO₂ emitted, making these eruptions net carbon sinks on centennial timescales with high probability (90-100%).
meta.observable: ratio of SOC buried (tons C) to CO₂ emitted (as tons C)
